nodes.label: sem:Literature:hopf-classes
nodes.title: The Hopf classes and their synthetic normalization
nodes.display_title: Prop 3.3: The Hopf classes and their synthetic normalization
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{Adams58}, Lem. 2.3; \cite{LWX126}, Prop. 3.16.)\par{}

The classical maps $\eta$ and $\nu$ are detected by the nonzero permanent cycles $h_1\in E_2^{1,2}$ and $h_2\in E_2^{1,4}$, respectively. The normalized synthetic lift $\eta\in\pi_{1,2}S^{0,0}$ has filtration exponent one, first-quotient label $h_1$, and realization equal to the classical $\eta$.

nodes.label: sem:Literature:theta-five
nodes.title: A detected Kervaire class in stem 62
nodes.display_title: Prop 3.4: A detected Kervaire class in stem 62
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BJMtheta5}, Thm. 2.1; \cite{Xu}, Cor. 1.3.)\par{}

There is a classical class $\theta_5\in\pi_{62}S^0$ of order two detected by the nonzero permanent cycle $h_5^2\in E_2^{2,64}$. Fix such a class. There is a synthetic lift $a\in\pi_{62,64}S^{0,0}$ with first-quotient label $h_5^2$ and $\operatorname{Re}(a)=\theta_5$.

nodes.label: sem:Literature:theta-indeterminacy
nodes.title: The 2-primary stem and the filtration of choices
nodes.display_title: Prop 3.5: The 2-primary stem and the filtration of choices
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{IWX}, Table 1; \cite{LWX126}, proof of Lem. 7.10.)\par{}

Every class $a\in\pi_{62}S^0$ annihilated by a power of two satisfies $2a=0$. If $a,b\in\pi_{62}S^0$ are detected by $h_5^2$, then $a-b$ has Adams filtration at least six.

nodes.title: The chosen tmf object, algebra, and unit
nodes.display_title: Def 3.8: The chosen tmf object, algebra, and unit
nodes.body:
(Project construction; cf.\ \cite{BR21}, §0.1.)\par{}

Let $\mathit{tmf}$ be the classical spectrum of topological modular forms, with its algebra structure and unit $u:S^0\to\mathit{tmf}$. Fix an isomorphism $\mathit{tmf}\cong D$ carrying $u$ to the unit of the detector $D$.

nodes.label: sem:Literature:tmf-convergence
nodes.title: Connectivity, finite type, and convergence for tmf
nodes.display_title: Prop 3.9: Connectivity, finite type, and convergence for tmf
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BR21}, §1.2.)\par{}

The spectrum $\mathit{tmf}$ is connective and has finite mod-two homology in each degree. Its classical Adams tower converges to its homotopy groups with their Adams filtration. Transport along $\mathit{tmf}\cong D$ preserves tower lifts and associated-graded representatives.

nodes.label: sem:Literature:kappa-detection
nodes.title: The class g and the detection of bar-kappa
nodes.display_title: Prop 3.10: The class g and the detection of bar-kappa
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BR21}, Thm. 11.61(20).)\par{}

The group $E_2^{4,24}(S^0)$ has a unique nonzero element $g$. It detects a class $\bar\kappa\in\pi_{20}S^0$, which we fix.

nodes.label: sem:Literature:w-detection
nodes.title: The class Delta h-one g and the detection of w
nodes.display_title: Prop 3.11: The class Delta h-one g and the detection of w
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BR21}, Thm. 11.59.)\par{}

The group $E_2^{9,54}(S^0)$ has a unique nonzero element $\Delta h_1g$. It detects a class $w\in\pi_{45}S^0$, which we fix.

nodes.title: The tmf Hurewicz input in stems 62 and 125
nodes.display_title: Prop 3.12: The tmf Hurewicz input in stems 62 and 125

nodes.title: The power-operation differential and detector transport
nodes.display_title: Thm 3.13: The power-operation differential and detector transport
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BR21}, Thm. 5.18.)\par{}

For the tmf classes $v_2^{16}\in E_2^{16,112}$ and $\beta^5g\in E_2^{19,114}$,
\[d_3(v_2^{16})=\beta^5g.\]
Under $\mathit{tmf}\cong D$, the images of these classes satisfy the same differential.

nodes.label: sem:Literature:nu-page-coordinates
nodes.title: Weight coordinates on the synthetic Adams pages
nodes.display_title: Def 3.14: Weight coordinates on the synthetic Adams pages
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Thm. A.8.)\par{}

For $X$ in the chosen classical object family, weight shift induces isomorphisms
\[E_r^{s,t,w}(\nu X)\cong E_r^{s,t,w-1}(\Sigma^{0,-1}\nu X).\]
For $k\ge0$, the $E_2$ labels in tridegree $(s,t,t-k)$ are the classical labels in bidegree $(s,t)$. Under these coordinates, the map induced by $\lambda:\Sigma^{0,-1}\nu X\to\nu X$ lowers weight by one.

nodes.label: sem:Literature:free-lambda-range
nodes.title: The free-lambda comparison range
nodes.display_title: Thm 3.15: The free-lambda comparison range
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Thm. A.8 and Cor. A.9.)\par{}

For $r\ge2$ and $r-2\le t-w$, there is an isomorphism
\[E_r^{s,t,w}(\nu X)\cong E_r^{s,t}(X).\]
It preserves $E_2$ labels and commutes with $\lambda$ and the differentials. Its inverse gives classical lifts with the same differential and $\lambda$ compatibilities.

nodes.label: sem:Literature:lambda-inversion
nodes.title: The comparison obtained by inverting lambda
nodes.display_title: Def 3.16: The comparison obtained by inverting lambda
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{Pst}, Prop. 4.40; \cite{BHS}, Thm. A.8.)\par{}

Inverting $\lambda$ induces a morphism from the synthetic cycle-and-boundary data of $\nu X$ to the classical data. It preserves cycles, boundaries, and $E_2$ labels, commutes with $d_r$ for $r\ge2$, and carries multiplication by $\lambda$ to the identity. For $r-2\le t-w$, its page map is the preceding free-range isomorphism.

nodes.label: sem:Literature:finite-quotient-labels
nodes.title: The finite quotient E-two strip
nodes.display_title: Prop 3.17: The finite quotient E-two strip
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Cor. A.11.)\par{}

For $q>0$,
\[E_2^{s,t,w}(\nu X/\lambda^q)\cong
\begin{cases}E_2^{s,t}(X),&0\le t-w<q,\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\]
In the displayed strip, the quotient projection preserves labels and is an isomorphism on $E_2$.

nodes.title: Vanishing windows and inherited degeneration
nodes.display_title: Thm 3.19: Vanishing windows and inherited degeneration
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Thm. A.8 and Cor. A.11.)\par{}

For $r\ge2$, one has $E_r^{s,t,w}(
u X)=0$ when $t<w$. For $q>0$, one has $E_r^{s,t,w}(
u X/\lambda^q)=0$ when $t-w<0$ or $q\le t-w$. If the classical Adams spectral sequence of $X$ degenerates at $N$, then the synthetic Adams spectral sequence of $
u X$ degenerates at $N$.

nodes.label: sem:Literature:cycle-quotients
nodes.title: Classical cycles, boundaries, and common permanent representatives
nodes.display_title: Def 3.20: Classical cycles, boundaries, and common permanent representatives
nodes.body:
(Project construction; cf.\ \cite{LWX126}, Notation 3.10.)\par{}

Let $Z_r^{s,t}(X)$ and $B_r^{s,t}(X)$ be the classical cycle and boundary subgroups of $E_2^{s,t}(X)$, and let $Z_\infty=\bigcap_r Z_r$. A classical permanent representative is an element of $Z_\infty$; zero is allowed. The cycle and permanent quotients are the corresponding subquotients of $E_2^{s,t}(X)$.

nodes.label: sem:Literature:infinite-nu-window
nodes.title: The infinite page of nu X and its labels
nodes.display_title: Prop 3.21: The infinite page of nu X and its labels
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Cor. A.9.)\par{}

For $X$ in the chosen classical object family,
\[E_\infty^{s,t,w}(\nu X)\cong
\begin{cases}Z_\infty^{s,t}(X)/B_{1+t-w}^{s,t}(X),&w\le t,\\0,&t<w.\end{cases}\]
This is a linear isomorphism carrying the infinite representative of an $E_2$ label to its permanent-cycle quotient class.

nodes.label: sem:Literature:infinite-finite-window
nodes.title: The infinite page of a finite lambda quotient
nodes.display_title: Prop 3.22: The infinite page of a finite lambda quotient
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Cor. A.11.)\par{}

For $q>0$,
\[E_\infty^{s,t,w}(\nu X/\lambda^q)\cong
\begin{cases}Z_{q-t+w}^{s,t}(X)/B_{1+t-w}^{s,t}(X),&0\le t-w<q,\\0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases}\]
This is a linear isomorphism compatible with labels and the quotient projection.

nodes.label: sem:Literature:infinite-shift
nodes.title: Shift comparison and naturality at infinity
nodes.display_title: Prop 3.23: Shift comparison and naturality at infinity
nodes.body:
(Project construction; cf.\ \cite{LWX126}, Rem. 3.14.)\par{}

For $k\ge0$, the shift $(0,-k)$ induces a filtered comparison and an $E_\infty$ comparison, natural in morphisms between objects in the chosen synthetic family. Composing with the map $\lambda^k$ gives the weight-lowering maps on the untruncated and finite-quotient infinite pages. At $k=0$ these maps are identities.

nodes.label: sem:Literature:infinite-lambda
nodes.title: Lambda on infinite-page quotient coordinates
nodes.display_title: Prop 3.24: Lambda on infinite-page quotient coordinates
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{LWX126}, Rem. 3.14.)\par{}

Under the infinite-page presentations, multiplication by $\lambda^k$ induces the natural map between classical cycle/boundary quotients. For $\nu X$, assume $w\le t$. For finite quotients, assume $k<q$ and $0\le t-w<q-k$; the source has length $q-k$ and weight $w$, and the target has length $q$ and weight $w-k$.

nodes.label: sem:Literature:infinite-restriction
nodes.title: Restriction between infinite-page windows
nodes.display_title: Prop 3.25: Restriction between infinite-page windows
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{LWX126}, Rem. 3.14.)\par{}

For $0<i\le j$ and $0\le t-w<i$, restriction $
u X/\lambda^j	o
u X/\lambda^i$ induces the natural map between the cycle/boundary quotients. Projection from $
u X$ to a positive-length finite quotient carries a permanent-cycle quotient class to its finite-cycle quotient class in the common strip.

nodes.label: sem:Literature:weight-epimorphisms
nodes.title: Weight maps are the actual lambda maps
nodes.display_title: Thm 3.26: Weight maps are the actual lambda maps
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Cor. A.9.)\par{}

For $w_1\le w_2\le t$, the weight map from $w_2$ to $w_1$ on $E_\infty(\nu X)$ is induced by $\lambda^{w_2-w_1}$. In quotient coordinates it preserves the permanent representative and enlarges the boundary subgroup. This map is an epimorphism. Thus multiplication by $\lambda^k$ on $E_\infty(\nu X)$ is an epimorphism whenever the source weight is at most $t$.

nodes.label: sem:Literature:cofiber-and-lift
nodes.title: Synthetic cofibers and full lifts of maps
nodes.display_title: Thm 3.27: Synthetic cofibers and full lifts of maps
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{Pst}, Lem. 4.23; \cite{BHS}, Lem. 9.15.)\par{}

For a classical cofiber triangle, its image under $\nu$ is a synthetic cofiber triangle if and only if its mod-two homology sequence is short exact. If $f$ has Adams tower filtration at least $k$, it has a synthetic lift whose composite with $\lambda^k$ is $\nu f$. A positive-filtration connecting map admits such a lift as the connecting arrow of the lifted triangle. Two full lifts may differ by $\lambda$ torsion.

nodes.label: sem:Literature:normalized-cofiber
nodes.title: Normalized arrows and their actual cofiber comparison
nodes.display_title: Def 3.28: Normalized arrows and their actual cofiber comparison
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{LWX126}, Prop. 3.20.)\par{}

For a triangle in the chosen classical object family, let its normalized arrows be obtained from synthetic lifts by shifting through their filtration exponents. The cofiber triangle of the first normalized arrow is distinguished and has a cofiber comparison. Call the normalized arrows compatible when the triangle formed by all three arrows is distinguished.

nodes.title: Finite lifts and the Bockstein differential
nodes.display_title: Thm 3.30: Finite lifts and the Bockstein differential
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Thm. A.1(1) and Cor. A.11.)\par{}

Let $q>0$ and $x\in E_2^{s,t}(X)$. The label $x$ reaches $E_{q+1}$ if and only if its first-quotient class lifts to $\nu X/\lambda^q$. Here reaching a page allows zero and boundaries. A suitable lift has Bockstein label representing $d_{q+1}x$ in bidegree $(s+q+1,t+q)$, where the Bockstein is the boundary of this quotient tower.

nodes.label: sem:Literature:differential-rigidity
nodes.title: Classical and synthetic differentials with common labels
nodes.display_title: Thm 3.31: Classical and synthetic differentials with common labels
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Thm. A.8(3).)\par{}

For $r\ge2$, the classical relation $d_r(x)=y$ is equivalent to the synthetic labeled relation $d_r(x)=\lambda^{r-1}y$. More generally,
\[d_r(\lambda^k x)=\lambda^{k+r-1}y.\]
After a shift $(0,a)$, both sides have weight $t+a-k$.

nodes.label: sem:Literature:bhs-applicability
nodes.title: The complete-source hypotheses for untruncated BHS
nodes.display_title: Def 3.32: The complete-source hypotheses for untruncated BHS
nodes.body:
(Project construction; cf.\ \cite{BHS}, Def. A.12.)\par{}

An object satisfies the complete-source hypotheses if countable products exist, the Milnor map $1-\mathrm{shift}$ on the product of residual Adams-tower stages is invertible, and the tower admits a completion witness. Require also that the homotopy filtration is separated in every degree and that the canonical convergence identification holds for this tower.
nodes.chapter: Literature --- External theorems and comparison inputs

nodes.label: sem:Literature:complete-permanent-lifts
nodes.title: Permanent lifts and filtration on a complete source
nodes.display_title: Thm 3.33: Permanent lifts and filtration on a complete source
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Thm. A.1 and Cor. A.19.)\par{}

Assume the complete-source hypotheses. A classical label has a common infinite-cycle representative if and only if it is the first-quotient image of an untruncated synthetic class. For a class of bidegree $(m,w)$ and $w-m\le s$, Adams filtration at least $s$ is equivalent to divisibility by $\lambda^{m+s-w}$ from weight $m+s$.
nodes.chapter: Literature --- External theorems and comparison inputs

nodes.label: sem:Literature:complete-lifetime
nodes.title: Lifetime of a lift on a complete source
nodes.display_title: Thm 3.34: Lifetime of a lift on a complete source
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Thm. A.1(2a).)\par{}

Assume the complete-source hypotheses. Let $r\ge1$, and let a synthetic class $a$ have first-quotient label $x$. If $x$ has a common permanent representative and survives nontrivially to $E_{r+1}$, then $\lambda^{r-1}a\ne0$.
nodes.chapter: Literature --- External theorems and comparison inputs

nodes.label: sem:Literature:complete-detection
nodes.title: Detection and prescribed realization on a complete source
nodes.display_title: Thm 3.35: Detection and prescribed realization on a complete source
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Thm. A.1(2b),(3b).)\par{}

Assume the complete-source hypotheses. The realization of a synthetic lift of a nonzero permanent label $x$ is detected by $x$ in the classical tower. Conversely, if a classical class $a$ is detected by such an $x$, there is a synthetic class with first-quotient label $x$ and realization $a$.
nodes.chapter: Literature --- External theorems and comparison inputs

nodes.label: sem:Literature:complete-boundary-lift
nodes.title: A boundary has a suitably torsion lift
nodes.display_title: Thm 3.36: A boundary has a suitably torsion lift
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Thm. A.1(3a).)\par{}

Assume the complete-source hypotheses. If $r\ge2$ and a classical label $y$ has a common infinite-cycle representative and is hit on page $r$, then $y$ has a synthetic lift $a$ with $\lambda^{r-1}a=0$.
nodes.chapter: Literature --- External theorems and comparison inputs

nodes.label: sem:Literature:selected-lifts
nodes.title: The source-to-selected-model infinite-lift comparisons
nodes.display_title: Prop 3.37: The source-to-selected-model infinite-lift comparisons
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Thm. A.1 and Cor. A.19.)\par{}

For $X$ in the chosen classical object family, a classical label has a common infinite-cycle representative if and only if it is the first-quotient image of an untruncated class on $\nu X$. For a class of bidegree $(m,w)$ and $w-m\le s$, Adams filtration at least $s$ is equivalent to divisibility by $\lambda^{m+s-w}$ from weight $m+s$. A class on an object in the chosen synthetic family has zero realization if and only if some finite power of $\lambda$ annihilates it.
nodes.chapter: Literature --- External theorems and comparison inputs

nodes.label: sem:Literature:selected-realization
nodes.title: The selected-model realization comparisons
nodes.display_title: Prop 3.38: The selected-model realization comparisons
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Thm. A.1(2)--(3).)\par{}

Let $X$ belong to the chosen classical object family. A lift $a$ of a common permanent label $x$ surviving nontrivially to $E_{r+1}$ satisfies $\lambda^{r-1}a\ne0$ for $r\ge1$. If $x$ is a nonzero permanent label, it detects $\operatorname{Re}(a)$; each prescribed classical class detected by $x$ is the realization of such a lift. If a common infinite-cycle label $y$ is hit on page $r\ge2$, it has a lift annihilated by $\lambda^{r-1}$.

nodes.title: The distinguished synthetic theta-five for the criterion
nodes.display_title: Def 3.39: The distinguished synthetic theta-five for the criterion
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BurklundXu}, Prop. 7.19.)\par{}

Fix the distinguished class $\theta_5^{\mathrm{BX}}\in\pi_{62,64}S^{0,0}$ of order two and first-quotient label $h_5^2$. Let $\eta$ be the normalized synthetic Hopf class with label $h_1$. The products $\eta(\theta_5^{\mathrm{BX}})^2$ and $\lambda\eta(\theta_5^{\mathrm{BX}})^2$ use these choices.

nodes.display_title: Def 3.42: Exact tensor functors in the same synthetic category

(Adapted from \cite{Pst}, Prop. 4.2; \cite{May01}, TC1--TC2.)\par{}

Left and right tensoring by a synthetic object commute with suspension and preserve distinguished triangles. Equip both functors with these shift isomorphisms and exactness structures; together they define the May tensor context.

nodes.display_title: Thm 3.43: May push-pull data and the signed boundary identity
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{May01}, Lem. 4.6.)\par{}

For two cofiber triangles in the May tensor context, their tensor-product diagram admits May push-pull data and a signed boundary identity. If multiplication by two annihilates the relevant boundary image, the signed identity gives the corresponding unsigned identity.

nodes.label: sem:Literature:mapping-system
nodes.title: Mapping spectra and actual composition
nodes.display_title: Def 3.44: Mapping spectra and actual composition
nodes.body:
(Project construction; cf.\ \cite{Moss}, §1.)\par{}

Fix the closed tensor structure on the classical category and mapping spectra between objects in the chosen sphere family. Their Adams systems have composition pairings, common cycle products, units, and filtered abutment products. On spheres, composition agrees with sphere multiplication and its unit.

nodes.label: sem:Literature:moss-detection
nodes.title: Multiplicative detection in the mapping system
nodes.display_title: Prop 3.45: Multiplicative detection in the mapping system
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{Moss}, §1; \cite{BelmontKong2024}, Def. 2.3.)\par{}

The composite of two detected stable maps is detected by the product of their common infinite-cycle representatives. The filtered abutment product is stable composition. The mapping Adams towers in the chosen sphere family are weakly convergent.

nodes.label: sem:Literature:moss-indeterminacy
nodes.title: The full Massey indeterminacy coset
nodes.display_title: Thm 3.46: The full Massey indeterminacy coset
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{Moss}, §1.)\par{}

Let $r\ge3$ and let $a,b,c$ be composable labels in the mapping Adams system. If $x_0$ is a value of their page-$r$ Massey relation, then $x$ is another value if and only if $x-x_0$ belongs to the full Massey indeterminacy subgroup. All values have the page-$r$ Massey degree of $a,b,c$.

nodes.label: sem:Literature:moss-convergence
nodes.title: Moss convergence with both crossing conditions
nodes.display_title: Thm 3.47: Moss convergence with both crossing conditions
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{Moss}, Thm. 1.2.)\par{}

Let $W,X,Y,Z$ belong to the chosen sphere mapping family, and let $r\ge3$. Suppose the composable page-$r$ labels $a,b,c$ detect stable maps $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$, their adjacent page products vanish, and the corresponding stable composites vanish. Assume weak convergence of the two product towers and both of Moss's no-crossing conditions. There is a permanent member of the page-$r$ Massey relation detecting a stable class whose associated map belongs to the Toda relation of $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$. The Massey relation includes a defining system on page $r-1$.

nodes.label: sem:Literature:toda-relations
nodes.title: Toda witnesses and their indeterminacy
nodes.display_title: Def 3.48: Toda witnesses and their indeterminacy
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{ChristensenFrankland2017}, Def. 3.1 and Lem. 3.4.)\par{}

A triple Toda witness consists of a distinguished cofiber triangle, null composites, an extension over the cofiber, and a boundary equation giving its value. A witness implies composability. For composable data, witnesses exist, and their values form a coset of the full Toda indeterminacy subgroup. In the synthetic sphere, use the fixed shift identifications.

nodes.label: sem:Literature:toda-functoriality
nodes.title: Naturality, juggling, suspension, and tensoring for Toda relations
nodes.display_title: Prop 3.49: Naturality, juggling, suspension, and tensoring for Toda relations
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{ChristensenFrankland2017}, Lem. 3.5 and Lem. 5.12.)\par{}

Pre- and postcomposition carry Toda witnesses to the corresponding witnesses, and factors can be absorbed into the first and last entries. Juggling, shuffle, and suspension preserve the cofiber relations. A compatible functor sends a witness to a witness. Tensoring on either side does the same when equipped with exactness and shift compatibility.

nodes.title: Algebra structures on the positive lambda quotients
nodes.display_title: Def 3.53: Algebra structures on the positive lambda quotients
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{LWX126}, Rem. 3.4.)\par{}

For each $q>0$, equip $S^{0,0}/\lambda^q$ with a commutative algebra structure in the symmetric synthetic category whose unit is the quotient inclusion. Its multiplication and the sphere tensor comparison induce a bigraded product. Multiplication by a projected sphere class equals the sphere action.

nodes.label: sem:Literature:first-quotient-products
nodes.title: The first quotient identifies products with Ext products
nodes.display_title: Prop 3.54: The first quotient identifies products with Ext products
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{Pst}, Thm. 4.46 and Lem. 4.56.)\par{}

Under the first-quotient equivalence, multiplication of classes in bidegrees $(t-s,t)$ and $(t'-s',t')$ is the classical sphere $E_2$ product in bidegree $(s+s',t+t')$. The action of an untruncated sphere class on a first-quotient class agrees with the same product.

nodes.label: sem:Literature:filtered-product-detection
nodes.title: Filtration and detection of actual products
nodes.display_title: Prop 3.55: Filtration and detection of actual products
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{Moss}, §1; \cite{BHS}, Rem. 9.5.)\par{}

A sphere class of filtration at least $s$ acting on a class of filtration at least $s'$ gives a class of filtration at least $s+s'$. On each positive finite quotient, if the two classes are detected by specified $E_2$ labels, their action is detected by the product of those labels, with the corresponding degree identifications. The classical product of detected sphere classes is likewise detected by the product of their classical $E_2$ labels.

nodes.label: paper:3.1
nodes.title: Synthetic cofiber sequences and homology exactness
nodes.display_title: Prop 3.59: Synthetic cofiber sequences and homology exactness
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Prop. 3.1.)\par{}

\href{paper/main.tex.html#L759}{Source text}.

[{\cite{Pst} ([Lemma 4.23])}]
    Suppose that
    $$X\fto{f} Y\fto{g} Z$$
    is a cofiber sequence of spectra. Then
    $$\nu X\fto{\nu f}\nu Y\fto{\nu g} \nu Z$$
    is a cofiber sequence of ${\HF}$-synthetic spectra if and only if
    $$0\to {\HF}_*X\fto{{\HF}_*f} {\HF}_*Y\fto{{\HF}_*g} {\HF}_*Z\to 0$$
    is a short exact sequence.

nodes.label: paper:3.6
nodes.title: Synthetic Adams pages and differentials
nodes.display_title: Thm 3.60: Synthetic Adams pages and differentials
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Thm. 3.6.)\par{}

\href{paper/main.tex.html#L799}{Source text}.

[{\cite{BHS} ([Theorem A.8])}] 
    The synthetic Adams spectral sequence for $\nu X$
     $$\SynSS_2^{s,t,w}(\nu X)\Longrightarrow \pi_{t-s,w}(\nu X)$$
     has an $E_2$-page 
    $$\SynSS_2^{*,*,*}(\nu X) \cong E_2^{*,*}(X)\otimes \mathbb{F}_2[\lambda]$$
    with differentials
    $$d_r: \SynSS_r^{s,t,w}\to \SynSS_r^{s+r,t+r-1,w}.$$
    Here $E_2^{*,*}(X) \cong \Ext_A^{*,*}(X)$ is the classical Adams $E_2$-page of $X$. An element in $E_2^{s,t}(X)$ is viewed as having tridegree $(s, t, t)$ in $\SynSS_2^{s,t,t}(\nu X)$, and $\lambda$ is in tridegree $(0, 0, -1)$. Given a classical Adams differential $d_r^{\mathrm{cl}}(x)=y$, the corresponding synthetic differential is $d_r(x)=\lambda^{r-1}y$, which is $\lambda$-linear, and all synthetic Adams differentials arise in this way.
nodes.chapter: Literature --- External theorems and comparison inputs

nodes.label: paper:3.8
nodes.title: The Adams and $\lambda$-Bockstein spectral sequences
nodes.display_title: Thm 3.61: The Adams and $\lambda$-Bockstein spectral sequences
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Thm. 3.8.)\par{}

\href{paper/main.tex.html#L813}{Source text}.

[{\cite{BHS} ([Theorem A.1])}]
    The synthetic Adams spectral sequence for $\nu X$ is isomorphic to the $\lambda$-Bockstein spectral sequence (with no sign difference because we are working over $\bF_2$ here). More specifically, we have
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(1)] $E_2^{s,t}(X)\iso \pi_{t-s,t}(\nu X /\lambda)$.
        \item[(2)] If we have a classical Adams differential $d_rx=y$ for 
        $$x\in E_2^{s,t}(X)\iso \pi_{t-s,t}(\nu X /\lambda),$$
        then $x$ admits a lift to $\pi_{t-s,t}(\nu X/\lambda^{r-1})$ whose image under the $\tau$-Bockstein
        $$\nu X/\lambda^{r-1}\to \Sus^{1,-r+1}\nu X/\lambda$$
        is equal to $d_r(x)$.

nodes.label: paper:3.17
nodes.title: Synthetic lifts of distinguished triangles
nodes.display_title: Prop 3.65: Synthetic lifts of distinguished triangles
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Prop. 3.17.)\par{}

\href{paper/main.tex.html#L929}{Source text}.


    Suppose that we have a  distinguished triangle of spectra
    $$X\fto{f} Y\fto{g} Z\fto{h} \Sus X$$
    with $\AF(h)>0$, and consequently a short exact sequence on $\HF$-homology
    $$0\to H_*X\fto{H_*f} H_*Y\fto{H_*g} H_*Z\to 0.$$
    Then there exists a distinguished triangle of synthetic spectra
    $$\nu X\fto{\nu f}\nu Y\fto{\nu g} \nu Z\fto{\Sus^{0,-1}\hat h} \Sus^{0,-1}\nu \Sus X=\Sus^{1,0}\nu X$$
    such that $\nu h=\lambda \hat h$.

nodes.display_title: Prop 3.66: Distinguished triangles with filtration shifts
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Prop. 3.20.)\par{}

\href{paper/main.tex.html#L965}{Source text}.

Suppose that we have a distinguished triangle of spectra
    $$X\fto{f} Y\fto{g} Z\fto{h} \Sus X$$
    such that $e(f)+e(g)+e(h)=1$. Then we have a distinguished triangle of synthetic spectra
    $$\nu X\fto{\hat f} \Sus^{0,-e(f)}\nu Y\fto{\hat g} \Sus^{0,-e(f)-e(g)}\nu Z\fto{\hat h} \Sus^{0,-1}\nu \Sus X$$
    (For simplicity we often omit the suspensions before maps but keep the suspensions before spectra.)

nodes.label: paper:7.3
nodes.title: A synthetic criterion for the survival of $h_6^2$
nodes.display_title: Thm 3.68: A synthetic criterion for the survival of $h_6^2$
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Thm. 7.3.)\par{}

\href{paper/main.tex.html#L2117}{Source text}.

[Barratt--Jones--Mahowald, Burklund--Xu] 
\begin{enumerate}
 \item[(1)]
 \item[(2)]    The element $h_6^2$ survives to the $E_{r+3}$-page of the classical Adams spectral sequence if and only if for some $\theta_5$, 
 $$\lambda \eta \theta_5^2 = 0 \ \text{in} \ \pi_{125,125+4} S^{0,0}/\lambda^{r+1}.$$
 \item[(3)]   In particular, $h_6^2$ is a permanent cycle in the classical Adams spectral sequence if and only if for some $\theta_5$,
 $$\lambda \eta \theta_5^2 = 0 \ \text{in} \ \pi_{125,125+4} S^{0,0}.$$ 
 \end{enumerate}



\par The fixed-choice interfaces use the distinguished $\theta_5^{\mathrm{BX}}$ and a positive finite-page parameter. The normalized criterion at every admissible theta choice, including the zero-parameter case, is stated in \ref{sem:Main:any-choice-criterion}.

nodes.body:

Let $s,t,s^{\prime},t^{\prime}\in\mathbb N$ and let $x,y$ be first-quotient classes in bidegrees $(t-s,t)$ and $(t^{\prime}-s^{\prime},t^{\prime})$. The first-quotient image of their algebra product equals the Ext product of their images, in bidegree $(s+s^{\prime},t+t^{\prime})$.

nodes.label: frontier:Literature:b8fc8580677d
nodes.title: Projection and lambda on infinite-page windows
nodes.display_title: Thm 3.114: Projection and lambda on infinite-page windows
nodes.chapter: Literature --- External theorems and comparison inputs

nodes.label: frontier:Literature:b4eb6770b658
nodes.title: Quotient multiplication and the sphere action
nodes.display_title: Thm 3.115: Quotient multiplication and the sphere action
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{LWX126}, Remark 3.4.)\par{}

Let $q>0$, $x\in\pi_{m,n}S^{0,0}$ and $y\in\pi_{k,l}(S^{0,0}/\lambda^q)$, with all four indices integral. Multiplication of the quotient image of $x$ by $y$ equals the sphere action $x\cdot y$.
nodes.chapter: Literature --- External theorems and comparison inputs

nodes.label: frontier:Literature:00344e96581e
nodes.title: Realization of lambda and the unit
nodes.display_title: Thm 3.116: Realization of lambda and the unit
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{Pst}, Prop. 4.40.)\par{}

For all $m,w\in\mathbb Z$ and $k\in\mathbb N$, realization carries $\lambda^k:S^{m,w-k}\to S^{m,w}$ to the identity in sphere coordinates. At $(m,w)=(0,0)$, the sphere isomorphism agrees with the composite of the zero-shift identification, the inverse $\nu$--realization isomorphism, and the realization of the synthetic unit isomorphism.
nodes.chapter: Literature --- External theorems and comparison inputs

nodes.label: frontier:Literature:636e4c89b3e4
nodes.title: Restriction between finite infinite-page windows
nodes.display_title: Thm 3.117: Restriction between finite infinite-page windows
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{LWX126}, Remark 3.14.)\par{}

Let $X$ belong to the chosen classical family, $0<i\le j$, and $0\le t-w<i$. Under the infinite-page window equivalences, restriction $\nu X/\lambda^j\to\nu X/\lambda^i$ induces the natural map\[Z_{j-t+w}^{s,t}/B_{1+t-w}^{s,t}\longrightarrow Z_{i-t+w}^{s,t}/B_{1+t-w}^{s,t}.\]
nodes.chapter: Literature --- External theorems and comparison inputs

nodes.label: frontier:Literature:98ed1948c077
nodes.title: The Bockstein represents the classical differential
nodes.display_title: Thm 3.118: The Bockstein represents the classical differential
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Thm. A.1(1c).)\par{}

Let $X$ belong to the chosen classical family, $q>0$, and $x\in E_2^{s,t}(X)$ reach $E_{q+1}$. There exists a lift $a\in\pi_{t-s,t}(\nu X/\lambda^q)$ restricting to the first-quotient class of $x$ such that the Bockstein label of $a$ represents $d_{q+1}x\in E_{q+1}^{s+q+1,t+q}(X)$.
nodes.chapter: Literature --- External theorems and comparison inputs

nodes.label: frontier:Literature:75582be1124c
nodes.title: The Hopf-invariant-one differentials
nodes.display_title: Thm 3.119: The Hopf-invariant-one differentials
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Introduction.)\par{}

For every $j\in\mathbb N$ with $j\ge4$, there is a nonzero differential\[d_2(h_j)=h_0h_{j-1}^2\in E_2^{3,1+2^j}(S^0).\]
nodes.chapter: Literature --- External theorems and comparison inputs

nodes.label: frontier:Literature:a4a50b59a6e9
nodes.title: The degree-two map and the realization kernel
nodes.display_title: Thm 3.120: The degree-two map and the realization kernel
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Prop. A.20(9).)\par{}

One has $\lambda[h_0]=2$ in the synthetic sphere. For every object $X$ in the chosen synthetic family and $a\in\pi_{m,w}X$, realization sends $a$ to zero if and only if $\lambda^k a=0$ for some $k\in\mathbb N$.
nodes.chapter: Literature --- External theorems and comparison inputs

nodes.label: frontier:Literature:48d4b249a919
nodes.title: The first-quotient label of eta
nodes.display_title: Thm 3.121: The first-quotient label of eta
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{LWX126}, Notation 7.2.)\par{}

The first-quotient image of the normalized synthetic class $\eta\in\pi_{1,2}S^{0,0}$ is $h_1\in E_2^{1,2}(S^0)$.

nodes.label: frontier:Literature:becf9ec11fa8
nodes.title: The h-zero eta relation
nodes.display_title: Thm 3.122: The h-zero eta relation
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BHS}, Prop. A.20(0).)\par{}

In the synthetic sphere, $[h_0]\eta=0$.

nodes.title: The order and label of BX theta-five
nodes.display_title: Thm 3.123: The order and label of BX theta-five
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BurklundXu}, Prop. 7.19.)\par{}

The distinguished class $\theta_5^{\mathrm{BX}}\in\pi_{62,64}S^{0,0}$ satisfies $2\theta_5^{\mathrm{BX}}=0$ and has first-quotient label $h_5^2$.

nodes.title: The tmf power-operation differential
nodes.display_title: Thm 3.124: The tmf power-operation differential
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{BR21}, Thm. 5.18.)\par{}

The tmf labels in bidegrees $(16,112)$ and $(19,114)$ satisfy\[d_3(v_2^{16})=\beta^5g.\]

The total boundary of the first-quotient class labeled $h_6^2$ is $\lambda\eta(\theta_5^{\mathrm{BX}})^2$.

nodes.label: sem:Computation:archive-labels
nodes.title: Archived labels and their bidegrees
nodes.display_title: Def 4.1: Archived labels and their bidegrees
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LinProgram}, archived sphere generators.)\par
The selected labels $h_i,g,e_0,\Delta h_1g,\Delta h_6g,Md_0,[B_4],b$ and $x_{n,s,j}$ carry their exact archived index, name and Adams bidegree $(s,t)$. A generator catalogue records every generator and its degree; a source monomial is formed from its unit, generators and degree-preserving products.
nodes.chapter: E2Computation --- The E2 Page and Algebraic Inputs

nodes.label: sem:Computation:source-presentation
nodes.title: The source presentation and complete archive
nodes.display_title: Def 4.2: The source presentation and complete archive
nodes.body: A source presentation consists of bigraded $\mathbb F_2$-modules, specified bilinear products, a unit element and the named atoms. A sphere archive specifies its complete generator list, the exact identification of every atom, and every basis monomial in each bidegree. Evaluation of a monomial uses these same products and generator values.
nodes.chapter: E2Computation --- The E2 Page and Algebraic Inputs

nodes.label: sem:Computation:fixed-archive
nodes.title: The fixed sphere archive
nodes.display_title: Def 4.3: The fixed sphere archive
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LinProgram}, archived sphere basis.)\par
Fix the project generator catalogue, atom indices, basis counts and basis monomials. The atom index determines the archived generator and its prescribed degree.
nodes.chapter: E2Computation --- The E2 Page and Algebraic Inputs

nodes.label: sem:Computation:source-components
nodes.title: The fixed source components and products
nodes.display_title: Def 4.4: The fixed source components and products
nodes.body: The fixed source object has components $P^{s,t}$ over $\mathbb F_2$, bilinear maps $P^{s,t}\times P^{s\prime,t\prime}\to P^{s+s\prime,t+t\prime}$, a unit in degree $(0,0)$ and its prescribed atom in each named degree. For each atom, its selected generator has the prescribed bidegree and value.
nodes.chapter: E2Computation --- The E2 Page and Algebraic Inputs

nodes.label: sem:Computation:source-basis
nodes.title: Complete source coordinates
nodes.display_title: Def 4.5: Complete source coordinates
nodes.body:
For $s,t\in\mathbb N$ and $t\leq261$, the source coordinates are a linear equivalence
\[P^{s,t}\cong\bigoplus_{i<\operatorname{basisCount}(s,t)}\mathbb F_2.\]
The inverse of each coordinate unit vector is the value of the corresponding archived monomial. In particular, the archived monomials form a basis of $P^{s,t}$.
nodes.chapter: E2Computation --- The E2 Page and Algebraic Inputs

nodes.label: sem:Computation:bounded-comparison
nodes.title: The bounded comparison
nodes.display_title: Def 4.6: The bounded comparison
nodes.body: For $s,t\in\mathbb N$ and $t\leq261$, the fixed comparison is a linear equivalence from $P^{s,t}$ to the actual sphere $E_2^{s,t}$. A sphere presentation requires the comparison to preserve the specified unit and every product of total degree $t+t\prime\leq261$, and to identify the selected $h_i$ with the fixed standard classes.
nodes.chapter: E2Computation --- The E2 Page and Algebraic Inputs

nodes.label: sem:Computation:multiplicative-comparison
nodes.title: Products and the unit under comparison
nodes.display_title: Thm 4.7: Products and the unit under comparison
nodes.body:
If $t+t\prime\leq261$, then
\[c(xy)=c(x)c(y),\qquad c(1)=1.\]
The comparison is $\mathbb F_2$-linear.
nodes.chapter: E2Computation --- The E2 Page and Algebraic Inputs

nodes.label: sem:Computation:standard-atoms
nodes.title: Identification of the standard atoms
nodes.display_title: Thm 4.8: Identification of the standard atoms
nodes.body: For $i=0,1,2,4,5,6$, the source atom $h_i$ is sent to the designated standard class $h_i\in E_2^{1,2^i}$. For every archived atom $a$, define its page class by $c(a)$.
nodes.chapter: E2Computation --- The E2 Page and Algebraic Inputs

nodes.label: sem:Computation:actual-coordinates
nodes.title: Coordinates on the actual page
nodes.display_title: Thm 4.9: Coordinates on the actual page
nodes.body:
For $t\leq261$, composition of the inverse comparison with the source coordinates gives
\[E_2^{s,t}\cong\bigoplus_{i<\operatorname{basisCount}(s,t)}\mathbb F_2.\]
Its inverse sends each unit vector to the image of the same archived monomial. Pulling that vector back by the comparison recovers the original source monomial.
nodes.chapter: E2Computation --- The E2 Page and Algebraic Inputs

nodes.label: sem:Computation:h6-square-calibration
nodes.title: Calibration of the Kervaire class
nodes.display_title: Thm 4.10: Calibration of the Kervaire class
nodes.body: The source product of the archived $h_6$ with itself maps to the designated actual class $h_6^2\in E_2^{2,128}$.
nodes.chapter: E2Computation --- The E2 Page and Algebraic Inputs

u$ be the cofiber of the fixed map $

nodes.body: The archived detector has bigraded $\mathbb F_2$-components, selected elements $v_2^{16}$ and $B_{19,114}$ in degrees $(16,112)$ and $(19,114)$, and a comparison with the actual detector $E_2$ for $t\leq261$. The two selected elements agree, under that comparison, with the fixed literature labels transported by the prescribed detector isomorphism.

nodes.label: sem:Computation:table-coordinate-syntax
nodes.title: Finite table coordinates
nodes.display_title: Def 4.23: Finite table coordinates
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LinProgram}, archived finite tables.)\par
A table row specifies the sphere or $C\nu$, an Adams bidegree and an increasing list of coordinate indices. A row is coordinate-valid if its degree occurs in the table and its coordinate indices are strictly increasing and less than the tabulated dimension.
nodes.chapter: E2Computation --- The E2 Page and Algebraic Inputs
nodes.section: Finite coordinates and calibrated polynomial values

nodes.label: sem:Computation:table-realization
nodes.title: Realization and decoding of a table row
nodes.display_title: Def 4.24: Realization and decoding of a table row
nodes.body:
For $o=S^0$ or $C\nu$, write $b_{o;s,t,i}\in E_2^{s,t}(o)$ for the specified basis vectors. For the sphere, $t\leq261$ and $i<\operatorname{basisCount}(s,t)$, these are the inverse coordinate images of the unit vectors; set $b_{S^0;s,t,i}=0$ when either bound fails. A coordinate-valid list $I$ represents
\[\sum_{i\in I}b_{o;s,t,i}.\]
An invalid coordinate list represents no element. The basis is complete if there is a linear coordinate equivalence sending every $b_{o;s,t,i}$ to the corresponding unit vector.
nodes.chapter: E2Computation --- The E2 Page and Algebraic Inputs
nodes.section: Finite coordinates and calibrated polynomial values

nodes.label: sem:Computation:table-bases
nodes.title: Correctness of the finite table bases
nodes.display_title: Thm 4.25: Correctness of the finite table bases
nodes.body: For every degree listed in the finite archive, its specified basis is complete. On the sphere, its length equals the fixed archive basis count; on $C\nu$, correctness refers to the prescribed cofiber basis. For $t\leq261$, the complete sphere archive count equals the tabulated dimension in degree $(s,t)$.

nodes.label: sem:Computation:polynomial-values
nodes.title: Polynomial expressions and calibrated basis values
nodes.display_title: Def 4.26: Polynomial expressions and calibrated basis values
nodes.body: Let $G_{j;s,t}$ be the image in $E_2^{s,t}$ of archived generator $j$ when $t\leq261$ and $j$ has bidegree $(s,t)$, and set $G_{j;s,t}=0$ otherwise. Expressions are formed from $1$, the named atoms, the elements $G_{j;s,t}$ and products. Their values are computed in the sphere $E_2$-page. For each basis-value record $(e,i)$, the $i$th basis vector in the bidegree of $e$ equals the value of $e$.

nodes.display_title: Thm 4.27: The named table basis elements
nodes.body:
The sphere basis vectors satisfy
\[b_{S^0;11,133,1}=P,\qquad b_{S^0;12,134,0}=Q,\qquad b_{S^0;14,139,1}=T,\]
\[b_{S^0;10,134,4}=U,\qquad b_{S^0;13,137,1}=C,\qquad b_{S^0;13,137,2}=h_4x_{109,12}.\]
If $x\in E_2^{s,t}$, $y\in E_2^{s\prime,t\prime}$ and $t+t\prime\leq261$, then $xy=yx$. Moreover, $h_0h_1=h_1h_2=0$.

nodes.label: sem:E2Computation:two-line-exhaustive
nodes.title: Exhaustive standard products on the Adams second line
nodes.display_title: Thm 4.30: Exhaustive standard products on the Adams second line
nodes.body:
(Adapted from \cite{Adams60}, Theorem 2.5.1(2), p.~45.)\par{}

For every integer $t$ and nonzero $x\in E_2^{2,t}(S^0)$, there are natural numbers $i\leq j$ and a bidegree equation
\[
 (1,2^i)+(1,2^j)=(2,t)
\]
such that $x$ equals the corresponding transport of $H_{i,j}$. There is no upper bound on $t$, $i$ or $j$.

chapters.title: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws

nodes.label: sem:ProofTools:common-labels
nodes.title: Common cycle, boundary and permanent labels
nodes.display_title: Def 5.1: Common cycle, boundary and permanent labels
nodes.body: For a classical spectrum $X$, a common label in bidegree $(s,t)$ is an element of $E_2^{s,t}(X)$. For $c\geq1$, it is a level-$c$ cycle, respectively boundary, if it lies in $Z_c^{s,t}(X)$, respectively $B_c^{s,t}(X)$. A permanent label is an element of $Z_\infty^{s,t}(X)$; the zero label is included.
nodes.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws

nodes.label: sem:ProofTools:congruence-and-differential
nodes.title: Congruence and differential equations
nodes.display_title: Def 5.2: Congruence and differential equations
nodes.body: For $c\geq1$, labels $x,y\in E_2^{s,t}(X)$ are congruent at level $c$ if $x-y\in B_c^{s,t}(X)$. For $r\geq2$, the equation $d_r(x)=y$ means that $x$ and $y$ represent classes on page $r$ and their classes satisfy the Adams differential equation, with source bidegree $(s,t)$ and target bidegree $(s+r,t+r-1)$. The target may be zero.
nodes.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws

nodes.label: sem:ProofTools:cycle-reaches
nodes.title: Cycles and representatives on later pages
nodes.display_title: Thm 5.3: Cycles and representatives on later pages
nodes.body: For $r\geq2$, a common label lies in $Z_{r-1}$ if and only if it reaches page $r$. If $x$ represents $x_r$ on page $r$ and $y-x\in B_{r-1}$, then $y$ represents $x_r$. If $d_r(x)=y$ and $y'-y\in B_{r-1}$, then $d_r(x)=y'$.
nodes.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws

nodes.label: sem:ProofTools:boundary-calculus
nodes.title: Boundary and cycle calculus
nodes.display_title: Thm 5.4: Boundary and cycle calculus
nodes.body: For $c\geq1$, $B_c\subseteq Z_c$, and $B_1=0$. If a common label represents zero on page $r\geq2$, it lies in $B_{r-1}$. Projection of a common cycle to the initial page recovers its $E_2$-label.
nodes.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws

nodes.label: sem:ProofTools:page-naturality
nodes.title: Composition and infinite representatives
nodes.display_title: Thm 5.5: Composition and infinite representatives
nodes.body: For composable synthetic maps $f$ and $g$, their induced page maps satisfy $(g\circ f)_r=g_r\circ f_r$. If $x$ represents an infinite-page class $e$, then $f_2(x)$ represents $f_\infty(e)$.
nodes.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws

nodes.label: sem:ProofTools:finite-correction
nodes.title: Finite correction of a residual
nodes.display_title: Thm 5.6: Finite correction of a residual
nodes.body:
Let $A,A',B$ be abelian groups, $N\in\mathbb N$, and $\rho:A'\to A$ and $g:A\to B$ homomorphisms, let $E_k\leq A$, $L_k\leq A'$ with $L$ decreasing, and let $T\leq B$. Suppose that for each $s\leq k<s+N$, a residual $\delta\in E_k$ can either be corrected by some $\varepsilon\in L_k$ so that $\delta-\rho\varepsilon\in E_{k+1}$, or already satisfies $g\delta\in T$. Suppose also that $g(E_{s+N})\subseteq T$. If $\alpha_0-\rho\alpha\in E_s$, there is $\alpha'$ with
\[\alpha'-\alpha\in L_s,\qquad g(\alpha_0-\rho\alpha')\in T.\]
nodes.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws

nodes.label: sem:ProofTools:finite-reflection
nodes.title: Reflection along a finite filtration interval
nodes.display_title: Thm 5.7: Reflection along a finite filtration interval
nodes.body: Let $B',B$ be abelian groups, $N\in\mathbb N$, and $\rho:B'\to B$ a homomorphism. Let $E$ be a decreasing filtration on $B$, and let $L_k\leq B'$. Suppose that for $s\leq k<s+N$, $b\in L_k$ and $\rho b\in E_{k+1}$ imply $b\in L_{k+1}$. Then $b\in L_s$ and $\rho b\in E_{s+N}$ imply $b\in L_{s+N}$.
nodes.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws

nodes.label: sem:ProofTools:leading-grade
nodes.title: The first nonzero grade in a finite interval
nodes.display_title: Thm 5.8: The first nonzero grade in a finite interval
nodes.body:
Let $E_k$ be subgroups of an abelian group and let $N\in\mathbb N$. If $b\in E_s$ but $b\notin E_{s+N}$, then there exists $s\leq k<s+N$ with
\[b\in E_k\quad\text{and}\quad b\notin E_{k+1}.\]
nodes.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws

nodes.label: sem:ProofTools:infinity-graded
nodes.title: The infinite-page graded identification
nodes.display_title: Def 5.9: The infinite-page graded identification
nodes.body:
For a convergent synthetic Adams tower on $X$, let
\[E_\infty^{s,m+s,w}(X)\cong\operatorname{gr}^s\pi_{m,w}X\]
be its convergence isomorphism.
nodes.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws

nodes.label: sem:ProofTools:filtration-representatives
nodes.title: Filtration representatives and preservation
nodes.display_title: Thm 5.10: Filtration representatives and preservation
nodes.body:
Every element of $F^s\pi_{m,w}X$ has a representative in the filtration subobject $F^sX$. If $g:X\to Y$ is a map of convergent towers, then
\[g_*\bigl(F^s\pi_{m,w}X\bigr)\subseteq F^s\pi_{m,w}Y.\]
nodes.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws

nodes.label: sem:ProofTools:extension-representatives
nodes.title: Representatives for a tower extension equation
nodes.display_title: Thm 5.11: Representatives for a tower extension equation
nodes.body:
Let $g:X\to Y$ be a map of convergent towers. Fix $(m,w)$ and classes $x\in E_\infty^{s,m+s,w}(X)$ and $y\in E_\infty^{s+n,m+s+n,w}(Y)$. An extension equation of length $n$ from $x$ to $y$ holds if and only if $n\geq0$ and there are representatives
\[a\in F^s\pi_{m,w}X,\qquad b\in F^{s+n}\pi_{m,w}Y,\qquad g_*(a)=b\]
whose associated-graded classes correspond to $x$ and $y$ under the convergence isomorphisms.
nodes.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws

nodes.label: sem:ProofTools:grade-naturality
nodes.title: Naturality and the next-filtration ambiguity
nodes.display_title: Thm 5.12: Naturality and the next-filtration ambiguity
nodes.body:
Let $g:X\to Y$ be a map of convergent towers, $a\in F^s\pi_{m,w}X$ and $b\in F^s\pi_{m,w}Y$. If $g_*(a)=b$, their associated-graded classes satisfy $g_\infty([a])=[b]$. Conversely, this graded equality implies
\[b-g_*(a)\in F^{s+1}\pi_{m,w}Y.\]
If $g_\infty$ is injective in this degree and $g_*(a)\in F^{s+1}\pi_{m,w}Y$, then $a\in F^{s+1}\pi_{m,w}X$.
nodes.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws

nodes.label: sem:ProofTools:detection-transport
nodes.title: Transport and reflection of detection
nodes.display_title: Thm 5.13: Transport and reflection of detection
nodes.body: Let $g:X\to Y$ be a map of convergent towers. If $x$ detects $\alpha$ on $X$, then $g_2(x)$ detects $g_*(\alpha)$ on $Y$. Conversely, suppose that $g_\infty$ is injective in filtration $s$, that $x$ represents an infinite-page class, and that $\alpha\in F^s\pi_{m,w}X$. If $g_2(x)$ detects $g_*(\alpha)$, then $x$ detects $\alpha$.
nodes.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws

nodes.label: sem:ProofTools:filtration-gap
nodes.title: A vanishing strip identifies filtration bounds
nodes.display_title: Thm 5.14: A vanishing strip identifies filtration bounds
nodes.body:
Fix a convergent synthetic Adams tower on $X$, and let $s\leq t$. If every infinite-page component $(j,m+j,w)$ vanishes for $s\leq j<t$, then for every $\alpha\in\pi_{m,w}X$,
\[\operatorname{fil}(\alpha)\geq s\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\operatorname{fil}(\alpha)\geq t.\]
nodes.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws

sections.title: Finite lambda quotients and sphere labels

nodes.label: sem:ProofTools:finite-strip
nodes.title: The finite quotient strip
nodes.display_title: Thm 5.15: The finite quotient strip
nodes.body:
For $q>0$, the infinite page of $
u X/\lambda^q$ vanishes outside $0\leq t-w<q$. Every $\alpha\in\pi_{t-s,t}(
u X/\lambda^q)$ has filtration at least $s$. If $q\leq m+s-w$, an element of $\pi_{m,w}(
u X/\lambda^q)$ in filtration at least $s$ is zero.
nodes.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
nodes.section: Finite lambda quotients and sphere labels

nodes.label: sem:ProofTools:rho-injectivity
nodes.title: Injectivity of quotient reduction in the retained strip
nodes.display_title: Thm 5.16: Injectivity of quotient reduction in the retained strip
nodes.body: For $0<i\leq j$ and $t-w<i$, the quotient reduction $\rho:\nu X/\lambda^j\to\nu X/\lambda^i$ induces an injective map on the infinite-page component in tridegree $(s,t,w)$.
nodes.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
nodes.section: Finite lambda quotients and sphere labels

nodes.label: sem:ProofTools:finite-target-label
nodes.title: Finite target labels
nodes.display_title: Thm 5.17: Finite target labels
nodes.body:
For $q>0$ and $0\leq k<q$, let $y\in Z_{q-k}^{s,t}(X)$. Its finite target label at weight $t-k$ represents $e\in E_\infty^{s,t,t-k}(\nu X/\lambda^q)$ if and only if the finite-window comparison carries $e$ to the class of $y$ in
\[Z_{q-k}^{s,t}(X)/B_{1+k}^{s,t}(X).\]
nodes.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
nodes.section: Finite lambda quotients and sphere labels

nodes.label: sem:ProofTools:sphere-label-detection
nodes.title: Sphere labels and finite lambda detection
nodes.display_title: Thm 5.18: Sphere labels and finite lambda detection
nodes.body: The first-quotient comparison carries the first label of $y\in E_2^{s,t}(S^0)$ to $y$. Let $\alpha\in\pi_{t-s,t}(\nu S^0)$ have first-quotient image equal to this label, using the canonical zero-shift identification. For $q>0$ and $k\geq0$, the finite target label of $y$ in tridegree $(s,t,t-k)$ detects the image of $\lambda^k\alpha$ in $\nu S^0/\lambda^q$.
nodes.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
nodes.section: Finite lambda quotients and sphere labels

nodes.label: sem:ProofTools:shift-coherence
nodes.title: Suspension and composition coherence
nodes.display_title: Thm 5.19: Suspension and composition coherence
nodes.body:
Assume that suspension and bigraded shifts are coherent with the homotopy functors. The canonical isomorphism
\[\Sigma^{1,-q}Q\cong\Sigma(\Sigma^{0,-q}Q)\]
identifies the induced suspension and bigraded-shift maps. The inverse and composition isomorphisms for shifts induce the corresponding inverse and composition maps on homotopy groups.
nodes.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
nodes.section: Finite lambda quotients and sphere labels

nodes.label: sem:ProofTools:leibniz-law
nodes.title: The generalized Leibniz law
nodes.display_title: Def 5.20: The generalized Leibniz law
nodes.body:
Let $f:X\to Y$ and write $e=e(f)$. The generalized Leibniz law is the following implication. Assume $2\leq p\leq r$, $e\leq m\leq p-2+e$, $e\leq l$, and
\[x\in Z_{r-1}^{s,t}(X),\qquad y\in Z_{r-1-m+e}^{s+m,t+m}(Y),\]
\[x_\infty\in Z_\infty^{s+r,t+r-1}(X),\qquad y_\infty\in Z_\infty^{s+r+l,t+r+l-1}(Y).\]
Suppose that
\[d_r(x)=x_\infty,\qquad d_m^{f,E_p}(x)=y,\qquad d_l^{f,E_\infty}(x_\infty)=y_\infty.\]
Assume either that the first differential has no crossing on page $p$ or that the finite extension has no crossing, and assume that the infinite extension has no crossing. Then
\[d_{r+l-m}(y)=y_\infty.\]
nodes.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws

nodes.label: sem:ProofTools:mahowald-law
nodes.title: The normalized-triangle Mahowald law
nodes.display_title: Def 5.21: The normalized-triangle Mahowald law
nodes.body:
Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ\xrightarrow h\Sigma X$ be a distinguished triangle with $e(f)+e(g)+e(h)=1$, whose normalized synthetic maps form a compatible triangle. Put
\[n_1=n-e(f)\geq1,\quad m_1=m-e(g)\geq0,\quad l_1=l-e(h)\geq0,\quad r=n+m+l,\quad r'=r-m_1.\]
The normalized-triangle Mahowald law is the following implication. Suppose
\[x\in Z_{n_1}^{s+l,t+l-1}(X),\quad y\in Z_{m_1+1}^{s+l+n,t+l+n-1}(Y),\]
\[\bar x\in Z_{r-1}^{s,t}(Z),\qquad\bar y\in Z_\infty^{s+r,t+r-1}(Z).\]
Let $\widetilde x\in E_2^{s+l,t+l}(\Sigma X)$ desuspend to $x$ under the tower suspension comparison, and assume
\[d_l^{h,E_{r'}}(\bar x)=\widetilde x,\qquad d_r(\bar x)=\bar y,\qquad d_m^{g,E_{m_1+2}}(y)=\bar y.\]
Assume that the $h$-extension has no crossing or that the classical differential has no crossing on page $r'$. Then $x\in Z_{n+m+e(h)}^{s+l,t+l-1}(X)$ and there is $y'$ such that
\[d_n^{f,E_{n+m+1+e(h)}}(x)=y',\qquad y'-y\in B_{r'}^{s+l+n,t+l+n-1}(Y).\]
nodes.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws

nodes.label: sem:ProofTools:nonliftable-obstruction
nodes.title: The same-quotient nonliftable obstruction
nodes.display_title: Def 5.22: The same-quotient nonliftable obstruction
nodes.body:
Let $r_{\rm early}\leq r_{\rm late}$. A nonliftable obstruction is an extension of length $n-a-b$ for the normalized map in the $(r_{\rm early}-1)$-st quotient, in stem $t-s$ and weight $t+e(f)$, where
\[a,b\in\mathbb N,\qquad 0<a\leq r_{\rm early}-2,\qquad a+b\leq n.\]
Its source has filtration $s+a$ and lies outside the image of quotient reduction from the $(r_{\rm late}-1)$-st quotient on $E_\infty$; its target has filtration $s+n-b$ and is nonzero. The extension may be inessential.
nodes.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws

nodes.label: sem:ProofTools:finite-stretching-law
nodes.title: The finite stretching sufficient condition
nodes.display_title: Def 5.23: The finite stretching sufficient condition
nodes.body:
Suppose $2\leq r_{\rm early}\leq r_{\rm late}$ and
\[e(f)\leq n\leq r_{\rm early}-2+e(f).\]
The finite stretching law is the following implication: if
\[x\in Z_{r_{\rm late}-1}^{s,t}(X),\qquad y\in Z_{r_{\rm late}-1-n+e(f)}^{s+n,t+n}(Y),\qquad d_n^{f,E_{r_{\rm early}}}(x)=y,\]
and there is no nonliftable obstruction as above, then
\[d_n^{f,E_{r_{\rm late}}}(x)=y.\]

nodes.label: sem:ProofTools:nu-zero-layer
nodes.title: The zero-layer nu-cofiber Mahowald instance
nodes.display_title: Thm 5.24: The zero-layer nu-cofiber Mahowald instance
nodes.body:
In the fixed cofiber triangle for $
u$, take labels $x\in E_2^{8,133}(S^3)$, $y\in E_2^{11,136}(S^0)$, $ ar x\in E_2^{8,134}(C
u)$ and permanent $ ar y\in E_2^{11,136}(C
u)$. Require $x\in Z_2$, $y\in Z_1$, $ ar x\in Z_2$, the actual suspension label for $x$, the length-zero connecting extension on page $3$, $d_3( ar x)= ar y$, its specified no-crossing alternative, and the length-zero bottom-cell extension on page $2$. Then $x\in Z_3$ and there is an actual $
u$-extension of length $3$ on page $4$ from $x$ to some $y'$ with $y'-y\in B_3$.

sections.title: Synthetic boundary maps and their labels

nodes.label: sem:ProofTools:synthetic-boundary-labels
nodes.title: Synthetic boundary maps and weighted labels
nodes.display_title: Def 5.25: Synthetic boundary maps and weighted labels
nodes.body:
For $n>0$, the absolute connecting map of the quotient triangle is
\[\delta_n:
u X/\lambda^n\longrightarrow\Sigma^{1,-n}
u X.\]
For $0<n<m$, its finite version has target $\Sigma^{1,-n}(
u X/\lambda^{m-n})$. Using the suspension isomorphism of the quotient triangle, the source label of $x$ is $\lambda^a x$ in the $n$-th quotient. For a classical differential of length $r=k+1$ and $n\leq a+k$, its target label is the shifted $\lambda^{a+k-n}y$; the finite label is its image under the target quotient projection. A crossing of the absolute boundary on page $p$ is an essential extension in that same boundary ESS, with source filtration $u$ and target filtration $v$ satisfying $s<u\leq v\leq s+r$.

sections.title: Representative criteria and changing the page

nodes.label: sem:ProofTools:crossing-ranges
nodes.title: Higher-source extension ranges
nodes.display_title: Def 5.26: Higher-source extension ranges
nodes.body: Let $f$ be a map of convergent towers or filtered abelian groups. An extension from source filtration $s$ to target filtration $s+n$ has no higher-source crossing over $[u,s+n]$ if every extension with source filtration greater than $s$ and target filtration in $[u,s+n]$ has zero target label. All extensions, including inessential ones, occur in this quantification.
nodes.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
nodes.section: Representative criteria and changing the page

nodes.label: sem:ProofTools:representative-criterion
nodes.title: The full representative criterion
nodes.display_title: Thm 5.27: The full representative criterion
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Prop. 2.10.)\par{}

Fix a map of convergent towers and an extension equation of length $n$ from $x$ to $y$ in filtrations $s$ and $s+n$, and a threshold $u\leq s+n$. Absence of higher-source extensions whose target lies between $u$ and $s+n$ is equivalent to the following condition: every representative $a$ of $x$ whose image has filtration at least $u$ has image representing the specified $y$ in filtration $s+n$. For threshold $u=s$, the image-filtration premise is automatic. If $y=0$, the conclusion says that every such image has filtration at least $s+n+1$. A map increasing every filtration by at least $n$ satisfies this criterion. The same assertions hold for a homomorphism of abelian groups with decreasing filtrations, using representatives of the given associated-graded source class.

nodes.section: Representative criteria and changing the page

nodes.label: sem:ProofTools:correction-label
nodes.title: Finite correction labels
nodes.display_title: Def 5.28: Finite correction labels
nodes.body: For $f:X\to Y$ and $x'\in E_2^{s+a,t+a}(X)$, the finite correction label is the image of $\lambda^a x'$ under the shift comparison and quotient isomorphism into the normalized finite source quotient, in synthetic weight $t+e(f)$.

nodes.section: Representative criteria and changing the page

nodes.label: sem:ProofTools:nonliftable-or-crossing
nodes.title: A nonliftable short extension or a late crossing
nodes.display_title: Thm 5.29: A nonliftable short extension or a late crossing
nodes.body: Consider finite witnesses for the same $f,x,y,n$ on pages $r_{\rm early}\leq r_{\rm late}$. If the late witness is essential and the early one is inessential, then either a shorter early extension retains the original target and has a source in the earlier cycle set but outside the later cycle set, or the same late normalized extension spectral sequence has a nonzero higher-source crossing in the specified range. The first branch uses the actual correction label with $b=0$ and all length and cycle bounds.

nodes.section: Representative criteria and changing the page

nodes.label: paper:2.7
nodes.title: Crossings of extensions
nodes.display_title: Def 5.30: Crossings of extensions
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Definition 2.7.)


\begin{enumerate}
    \item[(1)] For $x\in E_\infty^{s,t}(X)$, we say that the an $f$-extension $d_n^{f}(x)=y$ has a crossing that hits Adams filtration $p$ for some $p \leq s+n$, if there exists an element $x^\prime\in E_\infty^{s+a,t+a}(X)$ with $a>0$ and an $f$-extension $d_m^{f}(x^\prime)=y^\prime$ for $0\neq y^\prime\in E^{s+a+m, t+a+m}_\infty(Y)$ such that
    $$p = \textup{AF}(y^\prime) = s+a+m\le \textup{AF}(y) = s+n.$$
    \item[(2)] We say that an $f$-extension $d_n^{f}(x)=y$ has no crossing that hits the range AF $\ge p$ if there does not exist an element $x^\prime\in E_\infty^{s+a,t+a}(X)$ with $a>0$ and an $f$-extension $d_m^{f}(x^\prime)=y^\prime$ for $0\neq y^\prime\in E^{s+a+m, t+a+m}_\infty(Y)$ such that
    $$p\le \textup{AF}(y^\prime) = s+a+m\le \textup{AF}(y) = s+n.$$
    \item[(3)] We say that an $f$-extension $d_n^{f}(x)=y$ has no crossing if it has no crossing that hits the range AF$\ge \AF(x) + 1$.
\end{enumerate}
nodes.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws

nodes.label: paper:2.10
nodes.title: Characterization of extensions without crossings
nodes.display_title: Prop 5.31: Characterization of extensions without crossings
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Proposition 2.10.)


    An $f$-extension from $x$ to $y$ has no crossing in the range $\AF\ge p$ if and only if for all $[x]\in \{x\}$ such that $\AF(f[x])\ge p$ we have $f[x]\in \{y\}$. In particular, we have
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(1)] An $f$-extension from $x$ to $y$ has no crossing if and only if for all $[x]\in \{x\}$ we have $f[x]\in \{y\}$.
        \item[(2)] An $f$-extension $d_n^{f}(x)=0$ has no crossing if and only if for all $[x]\in \{x\}$,
        $$\AF(f[x]) >\AF(x)+n.$$
        \item[(3)] If $\AF(f)=n$, then all $d^f_n$-differentials have no crossing in the $f$-ESS.
    \end{enumerate}
nodes.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws

nodes.label: paper:2.12
nodes.title: The extension theorem for a commutative square
nodes.display_title: Thm 5.32: The extension theorem for a commutative square
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Theorem 2.12.)


    Consider a homotopy commutative diagram of spectra
    $$\text{see the original commutative diagram}$$
    Suppose $m,n,l\ge 0$, $0<k\le m+l-n$,
    $$\begin{array}{ll}
        x\in E^{s,t}_\infty(X) & y\in E^{s+n,t+n}_\infty(Y),\\
        z\in E^{s+m,t+m}_\infty(Z) & w\in E^{s+m+l,t+m+l}_\infty(W),
    \end{array}$$
    and
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(1)] $d^{f}_{n}(x)=y$,
        \item[(2)] $d^{p}_{m}(x)=z$,
        \item[(3)] the differential in (1) or the differential in (2) has no crossing,
        \item[(4)] $d^{g}_{l}(z)=w$, and has no crossing that hits the range AF $\ge s+n+k$,
        \item[(5)] $d^{q}_{k-1} y=0$, and has no crossing.
    \end{enumerate}
    Then $d^{q}_{m+l-n}(y)=w$. (See Figure \href{paper/main.tex.html#L551}{original source}.)
\par\href{paper/diagrams/2.12.html}{Original diagrams and hypotheses}

nodes.label: paper:2.15
nodes.title: A square of extensions without crossings
nodes.display_title: Cor 5.33: A square of extensions without crossings
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Corollary 2.15.)


    Consider a homotopy commutative diagram of spectra
    $$\text{see the original commutative diagram}$$
    Suppose $m,n,l\ge 0$, 
    $$\begin{array}{ll}
        x\in E^{s,t}_\infty(X) & y\in E^{s+n,t+n}_\infty(Y),\\
        z\in E^{s+m,t+m}_\infty(Z) & w\in E^{s+m+l,t+m+l}_\infty(W),
    \end{array}$$
    and
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(1)] $d^{f}_{n}(x)=y$,
        \item[(2)] $d^{p}_{m}(x)=z$,
        \item[(3)] the differential in (1) or the differential in (2) has no crossing,
        \item[(4)] $d^{g}_{l}(z)=w$, and has no crossing.
    \end{enumerate}
    Then $d^{q}_{m+l-n}(y)=w$.
\par\href{paper/diagrams/2.15.html}{Original diagrams and hypotheses}

nodes.label: paper:2.16
nodes.title: Extensions in a commutative triangle
nodes.display_title: Cor 5.34: Extensions in a commutative triangle
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Corollary 2.16.)


    Consider a homotopy commutative diagram of spectra
    $$\text{see the original commutative diagram}$$
    Suppose $n,m\ge 0$, 
    $$x\in E^{s,t}_\infty(X), ~y\in E^{s+n,t+n}_\infty(Y), ~z\in E^{s+m,t+m}_\infty(Z)$$
    and
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(1)] $d^{f}_{n}(x)=y$,
        \item[(2)] $d^{p}_{m}(x)=z$,
        \item[(3)] the differential in (1) or the differential in (2) has no crossing.
    \end{enumerate}
    Then $d^{q}_{m-n}(y)=z$.
\par\href{paper/diagrams/2.16.html}{Original diagrams and hypotheses}

nodes.label: paper:2.17
nodes.title: Composition of extensions
nodes.display_title: Cor 5.35: Composition of extensions
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Corollary 2.17.)


    Consider a homotopy commutative diagram of spectra
    $$\text{see the original commutative diagram}$$
    Suppose $n,m\ge 0$, 
    $$x\in E^{s,t}_\infty(X), ~z\in E^{s+m,t+m}_\infty(Y), ~w\in E^{s+m+l,t+m+l}_\infty(W)$$
    and
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(1)] $d^{p}_{m}(x)=z$,
        \item[(2)] $d^{g}_{l}(z)=w$, and has no crossing.
    \end{enumerate}
    Then $d^{q}_{m+l}(x)=w$.
\par\href{paper/diagrams/2.17.html}{Original diagrams and hypotheses}

sections.title: Functoriality and exactness of extension spectral sequences

nodes.label: paper:2.18
nodes.title: Morphisms of extension spectral sequences
nodes.display_title: Cor 5.36: Morphisms of extension spectral sequences
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Corollary 2.18.)


    Consider a homotopy commutative diagram of spectra
    $$\text{see the original commutative diagram}.$$
    Assume $\ESS{p}_0^{*,*}=\ESS{p}_r^{*,*}$ and $\ESS{q}_0^{*,*}=\ESS{q}_r^{*,*}$ for some $r\ge 0$. Then 
    $$(d^p_r, d^q_r): E_\infty^{*,*}(X)\oplus E_\infty^{*,*}(Y)\to E_\infty^{*,*}(Z)\oplus E_\infty^{*,*}(W)$$
    induces a map from the $f$-ESS to the $g$-ESS.
\par\href{paper/diagrams/2.18.html}{Original diagrams and hypotheses}

nodes.section: Functoriality and exactness of extension spectral sequences

nodes.label: paper:2.19
nodes.title: Permanent cycles from a null composite
nodes.display_title: Cor 5.37: Permanent cycles from a null composite
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Corollary 2.19.)


    If the composition $g\circ f$ of two maps $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y\to Z$ is trivial, and $d_n^f(x)=y$ for $x\in E_\infty^{s,t}(X)$ and $y\in E_\infty^{s+n,t+n}(Y)$, then $y$ is a permanent cycle in the $g$-ESS, i.e., we have
    $d^g_m(y)=0$ for all $m\ge 0$.

nodes.section: Functoriality and exactness of extension spectral sequences

nodes.label: paper:2.20
nodes.title: Exactness and extension boundaries
nodes.display_title: Prop 5.38: Exactness and extension boundaries
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Proposition 2.20.)


    Suppose that the sequence of spectra
    $$X\fto{f}Y\fto{g}Z$$
    induces a sequence of homotopy groups
    $$\pi_*X\fto{\pi_*f}\pi_*Y\fto{\pi_*g}\pi_*Z$$
    that is exact in $\pi_*Y$. Then all permanent cycles in $E^{*,*}_\infty(Y)$ of the $g$-ESS are boundaries in the $f$-ESS.

sections.title: Synthetic boundary maps and extension differentials

nodes.label: paper:4.2
nodes.title: Extensions for $\lambda^n$ and $\rho$
nodes.display_title: Prop 5.39: Extensions for $\lambda^n$ and $\rho$
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Proposition 4.2.)\par

 
The only nonzero differentials in the extension spectral sequences for the maps $\lambda^n$ and $\rho$ from Notation~\href{paper/main.tex.html#L1009}{original source} are the $d_0$'s:
$$d^{\lambda^n}_0=\lambda^n \ \text{and} \ d^{\rho}_0=\rho.$$ 
As a result, these $d_0$'s have no crossings.
nodes.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
nodes.section: Synthetic boundary maps and extension differentials

nodes.label: paper:4.6
nodes.title: Boundary extensions from Adams differentials
nodes.display_title: Prop 5.40: Boundary extensions from Adams differentials
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Proposition 4.6.)\par


    Suppose in the classical Adams spectral sequence of $X$ we have $d_r(x)=y$, where $x\in Z_{r-1}^{s,t}(X)$ and $y\in Z_\infty^{s+r,t+r-1}(X)$. Consider the map
    $$\delta:\nu X/\lambda^n\to \Sus^{1,-n}\nu X/\lambda^{m-n}.$$
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(1)] If $r\ge n+1$, then we view $x$ as an element of 
        $$E_\infty^{s,t,t}(\nu X/\lambda^n)\iso Z_n^{s,t}(X),$$
        and $\lambda^{r-n-1} y$ as an element of 
        $$E_\infty^{s+r,t+r-1, t+n}(\nu X/\lambda^{m-n})\iso Z_{m-r+1}^{s+r,t+r-1}(X)/B_{r-n}^{s+r,t+r-1}(X).$$
        We then have
        $$d^{\delta}_r(x)=\lambda^{r-n-1}y,$$
        which is trivial if $r>m$.
        \item[(2)] If $r<n+1$, then we view $\lambda^{n+1-r}x$ as an element of 
        $$E_\infty^{s,t,t-n-1+r}(\nu X/\lambda^n)\iso Z^{s,t}_{r-1}(X)/B^{s,t}_{n+2-r}(X),$$
        and $y$ as an element of 
        $$E_\infty^{s+r,t+r-1, t+r-1}(\nu X)\iso Z_\infty^{s+r,t+r-1}(X).$$
        In this case, we have
        $$d^{\delta}_r(\lambda^{n+1-r}x)=y.$$
    \end{enumerate}

nodes.label: paper:4.10
nodes.title: $\lambda$ multiples of boundary extensions
nodes.display_title: Cor 5.41: $\lambda$ multiples of boundary extensions

nodes.section: Synthetic boundary maps and extension differentials

nodes.label: paper:4.14
nodes.title: Crossings of Adams differentials
nodes.display_title: Def 5.42: Crossings of Adams differentials
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Definition 4.14.)\par


    Suppose $r\ge n+1$ and $d_r(x)=y$, where
    $$x\in E_2^{s,t}(X), \hspace{0.5cm} y\in E_2^{s+r,t+r-1}(X).$$
    A crossing of $d_r(x)=y$ on the $E_{n+1}$-page refers to an essential Adams differential
    $$d_{r-a-b}(x^\prime)=y^\prime,$$
    where
    $$x^\prime\in E_2^{s+a,t+a}(X), \hspace{.5cm} y^\prime\in E_2^{s+r-b,t+r-b-1}(X),$$
    with $0<a\le n-1$ and $0\le b\le r-n-1$. See Figure \href{paper/main.tex.html#L1211}{original source}.
nodes.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws

nodes.label: paper:4.16
nodes.title: Adams crossings and boundary-extension crossings
nodes.display_title: Prop 5.43: Adams crossings and boundary-extension crossings
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Proposition 4.16.)\par


    The Adams differential $d_r(x)=y$ has a crossing on the $E_{n+1}$-page if and only if the corresponding $\delta_n$-extension
    $$d^{\delta_n}_r(x)=\lambda^{r-n-1}y$$
    for
    $$\delta_{n}:\nu X/\lambda^{n}\to \Sus^{1,-n}\nu X$$
    has a crossing.

sections.title: Extension witnesses on finite and infinite pages

nodes.label: paper:5.4
nodes.title: Extensions on the $E_r$-page
nodes.display_title: Def 5.44: Extensions on the $E_r$-page
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Definition 5.4.)\par


    Let $x\in Z^{s,t}_{r-1}(X)$ and $y\in Z^{s+n,t+n}_{r-1-n+e(f)}(Y)$ for some 
    $$e(f)\le n\le r-2+e(f).$$
    We say that there is an $(f,E_r)$-extension from $x$ to $y$, denoted by
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:b98be76a}
    d_{n}^{f,E_r}(x)=y
    \end{equation}
    if there exists a synthetic $\hat f_{r-1}$-extension
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:a020bad3}
        d_{n}^{\hat f_{r-1}}(x)=\lambda^{n-e(f)} y.
    \end{equation}
    where $x$ is viewed as an element of the subgroup (\href{paper/main.tex.html#L1290}{original source}) with $k=0$, and $\lambda^{n-e(f)} y$ is viewed as an element of the quotient group (\href{paper/main.tex.html#L1294}{original source}) with $k=0$. 

   We say that this $(f,E_r)$-extension in (\href{paper/main.tex.html#L1305}{original source}) is \emph{essential} if the corresponding synthetic $\hat f_{r-1}$-extension in (\href{paper/main.tex.html#L1309}{original source}) is an essential differential in the $\hat f_{r-1}$-ESS.
    
    For $r=\infty$, we similar define an $(f,E_\infty)$-extension using the corresponding synthetic $\hat f$-extension.
nodes.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
nodes.section: Extension witnesses on finite and infinite pages

nodes.label: paper:5.9
nodes.title: Crossings of $E_r$-extensions
nodes.display_title: Def 5.45: Crossings of $E_r$-extensions
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Definition 5.9.)\par


    A crossing of the $(f,E_r)$-extension $d_{n}^{f,E_r}(x)=y$ in (\href{paper/main.tex.html#L1305}{original source}) is defined as an essential $(f, E_{r-a})$-extension from some $x'\in Z_{r-1-a}^{s+a,t+a}(X)$ to 
    $$y'\in Z_{r-1-n+b+e(f)}^{s+n-b,t+n-b}(Y)\backslash B_{1+n-b-e(f)}^{s+n-b,t+n-b}(Y)$$
    (where $\backslash$ denotes the difference of sets and it means that $y'$ should survive to the classical Adams $E_{r-n+b+e(f)}$ page while it should not be hit by an Adams differential of length at most $1+n-b-e(f)$) for $0<a \le r-2$ and $0\le b\le n-a-e(f)$. See Figure \href{paper/main.tex.html#L1512}{original source}.
nodes.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
nodes.section: Extension witnesses on finite and infinite pages

nodes.label: paper:5.10
nodes.title: Crossings of $E_r$-extensions and synthetic extensions
nodes.display_title: Prop 5.46: Crossings of $E_r$-extensions and synthetic extensions
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Proposition 5.10.)\par


    An $(f,E_r)$-extension $d_{n}^{f,E_r}(x)=y$ (\href{paper/main.tex.html#L1305}{original source}) has a crossing if and only if the synthetic $\hat f_{r-1}$-extension $d_{n}^{\hat f_{r-1}}(x)=\lambda^{n-e(f)} y$ (\href{paper/main.tex.html#L1309}{original source}) has a crossing.
nodes.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
nodes.section: Extension witnesses on finite and infinite pages

nodes.label: paper:5.14
nodes.title: From infinity-page extensions to homotopy extensions
nodes.display_title: Prop 5.47: From infinity-page extensions to homotopy extensions
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Proposition 5.14.)\par

Consider $f: X\to Y$, $x\in Z_\infty^{s,t}(X)$ and $y\in Z_\infty^{s+n,t+n}(Y)$.
    Then
    $$d^{f,E_\infty}_n(x)=y$$
    implies that
    $$d^{f}_n(x+B_\infty^{s,t}(X))=y+B_\infty^{s,t}(Y).$$

nodes.section: Extension witnesses on finite and infinite pages

sections.title: The generalized Leibniz rule and Mahowald trick

nodes.label: paper:6.1
nodes.title: The generalized Leibniz rule
nodes.display_title: Thm 5.48: The generalized Leibniz rule
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Theorem 6.1.)\par

[Generalized Leibniz Rule]
    Let $f: X\to Y$ be a map between two classical spectra.
    Suppose that $2\le n\le r$, $e(f)\le m\le n-2+e(f)$, $l\ge e(f)$, and we have
    $$x\in Z_{r-1}^{s,t}(X), \hspace{0.5cm} y\in Z_{r-1-m+e(f)}^{s+m,t+m}(Y)$$
    $$x_\infty\in Z_\infty^{s+r,t+r-1}(X), \hspace{0.5cm} y_\infty\in Z_\infty^{s+r+l,t+r+l-1}(Y)$$
    and the following conditions hold:
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(1)] $d_{r}(x)=x_\infty$,
        \item[(2)] $d_{m}^{f,E_n}(x)=y$,
        \item[(3)] $d_{l}^{f,E_\infty}(x_\infty)=y_\infty$,
        \item[(4)] the differential in (1) has no crossing on the $E_n$-page or (2) has no crossing.
        \item[(5)] the differential in (3) has no crossing.
    \end{enumerate}
    Then we have an Adams differential
    $$d_{r+l-m}(y)= y_\infty.$$

nodes.label: paper:6.12
nodes.title: The generalized Mahowald trick
nodes.display_title: Thm 5.49: The generalized Mahowald trick
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Theorem 6.12.)\par

[Generalized Mahowald Trick] 
    Consider a distinguished triangle of spectra
    $$X\fto{f} Y\fto{g} Z\fto{h} \Sus X$$
    with $e(f)+e(g)+e(h)=1$.
    Suppose that $r=n+m+l$, $n_1=n-e(f)\ge 1$, $m_1=m-e(g)\ge 0$, $l_1=l-e(h)\ge 0$, and
    $$\begin{array}{ll}
        x\in Z_{n_1}^{s+l,t+l-1}(X), & y\in Z_{m_1+1}^{s+n+l,t+n+l-1}(Y),\\
        \bar x\in Z_{r-1}^{s,t}(Z), & \bar y\in Z_\infty^{s+r,t+r-1}(Z),
    \end{array}$$
    such that
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(1)] $d^{h,E_{r'}}_{l}\bar x=x$, where $r'=r-m_1=n_1+l_1+1$,
        \item[(2)] $d_r \bar x=\bar y$,
            \item[(3)] the $(h,E_{r'})$-extension in (1) has no crossing, or the Adams differential (2) has no crossing on the $E_{r'}$-page,
        \item[(4)] $d^{g,E_{m_1+2}}_{m}y=\bar y$.
    \end{enumerate}
    Then we have $x\in Z_{n+m+e(h)}^{s+l,t+l-1}(X)$ and
    $$d^{f,E_{n+m+1+e(h)}}_{n}x\equiv y \mod B_{r'}^{s+n+l,t+n+l-1}(Y).$$
    (See Figure \href{paper/main.tex.html#L1845}{original source}.)
nodes.chapter: ProofTools — Representatives, extensions and comparison laws
nodes.section: The generalized Leibniz rule and Mahowald trick

nodes.label: paper:6.20
nodes.title: Restriction of extensions to earlier pages
nodes.display_title: Prop 5.50: Restriction of extensions to earlier pages
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Proposition 6.20.)\par


    Suppose that we have an $(f,E_r)$-extension $d^{f,E_r}_n(x)=y$, where $x\in Z_{r-1}^{s,t}(X)$ and $y\in Z_{r-1-n+e(f)}^{s+n,t+n}(Y)$. Then for all $2\le r'<r$, we also have
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:dr'}
        d^{f,E_{r'}}_n(x)=y.
    \end{equation}

    Furthermore, if $d^{f,E_r}_n(x)=y$ is essential and $n\le r'-2+e(f)$, then (\href{paper/main.tex.html#L1983}{original source}) is inessential if and only if there exists some $0<a'\le n-e(f)$ and an element
    $$x'\in Z_{r'-1-a'}^{s+a',t+a'}(X)\backslash Z_{r-1-a'}^{s+a',t+a'}(X)$$
    such that
    $$d^{\hat f_{r'-1}}_{n-a'-b}(\lambda^{a'} x')=\lambda^{n-b-e(f)} y'$$
    for some $b\ge 0$.

nodes.title: Lifting extensions to later pages
nodes.display_title: Cor 5.51: Lifting extensions to later pages
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Corollary 6.23.)\par


    Suppose $r\ge r'$ and there exists an $(f,E_{r'})$-extension 
    $$d^{f,E_{r'}}_n(x)=y$$
    for $x\in Z_{r-1}^{s,t}(X)$ and $y\in Z_{r'-1-n+e(f)}^{s+n,t+n}(Y)$. Assume that this extension has no crossing of the form $d^{f,E_{r'-a}}_{n-a-b}(x')=y'$ for any $b>0$, $0<a\le n-e(f)$, and 
    $$x'\in Z_{r'-1-a}^{s+a,t+a}(X)\backslash Z_{r-1-a}^{s+a,t+a}(X).$$ 
    Under these conditions, we also have an $(f,E_{r})$-extension
    $$d^{f,E_{r}}_n(x)=y.$$
