nodes.label: frontier:ProofTools:003e9deb7ec5
nodes.title: Generalized Leibniz and Mahowald laws
nodes.display_title: Thm 5.52: Generalized Leibniz and Mahowald laws
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Theorems 6.1 and 6.12.)\par
Work in the fixed classical and synthetic Adams model.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $X,Y$ be classical spectra and $f:X\to Y$, and put $e=e(f)$. For every $p\in\mathbb N$ and $r,m,l,s,t\in\mathbb Z$ with
\[2\leq p\leq r,\qquad e\leq m\leq p-2+e,\qquad e\leq l,\]
let
\[x\in Z_{r-1}^{s,t}(X),\qquad y\in Z_{r-1-m+e}^{s+m,t+m}(Y),\]
\[x_\infty\in Z_\infty^{s+r,t+r-1}(X),\qquad y_\infty\in Z_\infty^{s+r+l,t+r+l-1}(Y).
\]
Suppose that
\[d_r(x)=x_\infty,\qquad d_m^{f,E_p}(x)=y,\qquad d_l^{f,E_\infty}(x_\infty)=y_\infty.
\]
Assume that the first differential has no crossing on page $p$ or that the finite extension has no crossing, and that the infinite extension has no crossing. Then
\[d_{r+l-m}(y)=y_\infty.
\]
Thus the generalized Leibniz law of \ref{sem:ProofTools:leibniz-law} holds for every $X,Y,f$.

\item Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ\xrightarrow h\Sigma X$ be a distinguished triangle with
\[e(f)+e(g)+e(h)=1,
\]
and assume that its normalized synthetic maps form a compatible triangle, as in \ref{sem:ProofTools:mahowald-law}. For every $n,m,l,s,t\in\mathbb Z$, put
\[n_1=n-e(f)\geq1,\quad m_1=m-e(g)\geq0,\quad l_1=l-e(h)\geq0,\quad r=n+m+l,\quad r'=r-m_1.
\]
Let
\[x\in Z_{n_1}^{s+l,t+l-1}(X),\qquad y\in Z_{m_1+1}^{s+l+n,t+l+n-1}(Y),\]
\[\bar x\in Z_{r-1}^{s,t}(Z),\qquad\bar y\in Z_\infty^{s+r,t+r-1}(Z).
\]
Let $\widetilde x\in E_2^{s+l,t+l}(\Sigma X)$ desuspend to $x$ under the classical tower suspension comparison. Suppose that
\[d_l^{h,E_{r'}}(\bar x)=\widetilde x,\qquad d_r(\bar x)=\bar y,\qquad d_m^{g,E_{m_1+2}}(y)=\bar y.
\]
Assume that the $h$-extension has no crossing or that the classical differential has no crossing on page $r'$. Then
\[x\in Z_{n+m+e(h)}^{s+l,t+l-1}(X)
\]
and there is $y'\in E_2^{s+l+n,t+l+n-1}(Y)$ such that
\[d_n^{f,E_{n+m+1+e(h)}}(x)=y',\qquad y'-y\in B_{r'}^{s+l+n,t+l+n-1}(Y).
\]
\end{enumerate}

(From \cite{LinProgram}, archived Adams calculation records.)\par
A claim row specifies a spectrum, source and target coordinate lists, a page $r$, and one of four predicates: a differential equation, reaching a finite page, a boundary bound, or the refutation of a differential equation. A valid row has $r\geq2$ and valid coordinates; an equation or refutation also requires $(s\prime,t\prime)=(s+r,t+r-1)$. Validity checks the record's syntax and degrees; the mathematical certification is stated separately.

nodes.display_title: Def 7.7: The exact second-line classification proposition
nodes.body:
\textit{(From \cite{LWX126}, Corollary 1.5.)}
For $x\in E_2^{2,t}$, let $L(t,x)$ mean that $x$ equals one of
\[
 h_0h_2,\quad h_0h_3,\quad h_2h_4,\quad h_1h_j\ (j\geq3),\quad h_j^2\ (0\leq j\leq6).
\]
Each equality includes its bidegree equation and transport in the actual sphere $E_2$ module. Define the proposition $C$ by
\[
 C\;:\!\Longleftrightarrow\;\forall t\in\mathbb Z\ \forall x\in E_2^{2,t},\quad
 x\text{ survives nontrivially to }E_\infty\ \Longleftrightarrow\ L(t,x).
\]
This entry defines the target; it does not prove $C$.

nodes.label: sem:Main:remark-7.4
nodes.title: Remark 7.4: normalization of the finite-quotient criterion
nodes.display_title: Rmk 7.10: Remark 7.4: normalization of the finite-quotient criterion
nodes.body:
\textit{(From \cite{LWX126}, Remark 7.4.)}
Let $q_n$ denote the quotient map to $S^{0,0}/\lambda^n$. For every $a\in\pi_{125,130}S^{0,0}$ and $n\geq0$,
\[
 q_n(a)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad q_{n+1}(\lambda a)=0.
\]
In particular, with $a=\eta(\theta_5^{\mathrm{BX}})^2$ this identifies the two quotient conditions
\[
 q_r\bigl(\eta(\theta_5^{\mathrm{BX}})^2\bigr)=0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 q_{r+1}\bigl(\lambda\eta(\theta_5^{\mathrm{BX}})^2\bigr)=0.
\]
\par\emph{Proof.} Exactness of the lambda cofiber sequence identifies $\ker q_n$ with the image of $\lambda^n$. Multiplication by $\lambda$ is injective on $\pi_{125,130}S^{0,0}$ in the fixed system. Thus $\lambda a=\lambda^{n+1}b$ is equivalent to $a=\lambda^n b$. Specializing $a$ gives the change of quotient convention used in \ref{paper:7.3}.



\href{paper/main.tex.html#L2127}{Original remark}.

nodes.label: sem:Main:remark-7.5
nodes.title: Remark 7.5: independence of the theta choice
nodes.display_title: Rmk 7.11: Remark 7.5: independence of the theta choice
nodes.body:
\textit{(From \cite{LWX126}, Remark 7.5.)}
For every $\theta\in\pi_{62,64}S^{0,0}$ satisfying $\operatorname{ThetaChoice}(\theta)$,
\[
 \lambda\eta\theta^2=\lambda\eta(\theta_5^{\mathrm{BX}})^2.
\]
In particular, this expression has the same value for any two admissible choices. It is the expression, rather than $\theta$ itself, that is independent of the choice.
\par\emph{Proof.} The stem-62 choice comparison places $\theta-\theta_5^{\mathrm{BX}}$ in filtration at least six. The exponent-two square identity therefore puts $\theta^2-(\theta_5^{\mathrm{BX}})^2$ in filtration at least twelve. The established eta-error estimate raises the filtration of its eta multiple to at least fifteen. This eta-product difference is annihilated by two and has zero detector image, so the established filtration-fifteen detection theorem makes it zero. Multiplying by $\lambda$ gives the claimed equality.



\href{paper/main.tex.html#L2133}{Original remark}.

nodes.label: sem:Main:boundary-formula
nodes.title: The total boundary at every theta choice
nodes.display_title: Thm 7.12: The total boundary at every theta choice
nodes.body:
\textit{(From \cite{LWX126}, Remark 7.5.)}
For every admissible $\theta\in\pi_{62,64}S^{0,0}$, the total boundary of the first-quotient class $h_6^2$ satisfies
\[
 \delta_1(h_6^2)=\lambda\eta\theta^2.
\]
Here $\delta_1$ is the connecting map for the first lambda quotient. In particular, $\lambda\eta\theta^2$ is independent of the admissible theta choice.
\par\emph{Proof.} Literature gives the boundary formula at $\theta_5^{\mathrm{BX}}$; \ref{sem:Main:remark-7.5} identifies its right-hand side with the expression at $\theta$.

nodes.label: sem:Main:any-choice-criterion
nodes.title: Normalization and choice transport of the literature criterion
nodes.display_title: Thm 7.13: Normalization and choice transport of the literature criterion
nodes.body:
\textit{(From \cite{LWX126}, Theorem 7.3 and Remarks 7.4--7.5; \cite{BurklundXu}, Proposition 7.19.)}
The literature criterion is recalled in \ref{paper:7.3}. On the fixed system its normalized form is as follows.
For every admissible $\theta$ and every natural number $r\geq0$,
\[
 h_6^2\text{ survives to }E_{r+3}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 [\lambda\eta\theta^2]=0\text{ in }S^{0,0}/\lambda^{r+1}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 P\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\lambda\eta\theta^2=0
 \text{ in the untruncated synthetic sphere}.
\]
\par\emph{Proof.} For $r\geq1$, apply the distinguished-choice literature criterion and then combine \ref{sem:Main:remark-7.4} with \ref{sem:Main:remark-7.5}. At $r=0$, $h_6^2$ survives to $E_3$ and every lambda multiple maps to zero in $S^{0,0}/\lambda$. The untruncated equivalence is the distinguished-choice literature criterion followed by \ref{sem:Main:remark-7.5}.

nodes.display_title: Def 7.15: The finite and untruncated detection predicates
nodes.body:
Let $x\in E_2^{s,t}$ and let $k\geq0$. For $n>0$ and

 a\in\pi_{t-s,t-k}(S^{0,0}/\lambda^n),
\]

nodes.display_title: Cor 7.17: Survivors on the Adams 2-line
nodes.body:
\textit{(From \cite{LWX126}, Corollary 1.5.)}


    On the Adams 2-line, the only non-trivial elements that survive in the Adams spectral sequence are:
    $$h_0h_2, \ h_0h_3, \ h_2h_4, \ h_1h_j \ (j \geq 3), \ h_j^2 \ (j \leq 6).$$




\par\emph{Proof.} Write any nonzero second-line class as a standard product using the exhaustive $E_2$ basis. Its third-page continuation restricts it to the corrected Adams--Lin--Leibniz candidates, including $h_0h_4$. Four exceptional mixed products support nonzero outgoing differentials, while HHR excludes squares of index at least seven. Conversely, the remaining products survive by the low-dimensional, Mahowald-family and Kervaire literature inputs, together with the main $h_6^2$ theorem.

nodes.display_title: Prop 7.19: The last differential and its detection conditions
nodes.body:
\textit{(From \cite{LWX126}, Proposition 7.8.)}


Exactly one of the following two statements is true:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item[(1)] The element $h_6^2$ survives to the $E_\infty$-page.
   
    \item[(2)] There is a nonzero classical Adams differential 
    $$d_{12}(h_6^2) = h_1h_4x_{109,12}.$$
\end{enumerate}
Furthermore, statement $(2)$ is true if and only if the following three statements are all true:
\begin{enumerate} 
    \item[(3)] \leavevmode  
    $$d_6(x_{126,8,4} + x_{126,8}) = 0.$$
    
    \item[(4)] There exists a $\theta_5$ such that 
    $\theta_5^2$ is detected by $\lambda^6 h_0^2x_{124,8}$. In particular, 
    $$\theta_5^2 = \lambda^6 [h_0^2x_{124,8}] \neq 0 \in \pi_{124,124+4}S^{0,0}$$
    for some $[h_0^2x_{124,8}]$.

    \item[(5)] There exists a homotopy class $[h_0^2x_{124,8}]$ such that
    $\lambda^3 \eta [h_0^2x_{124,8}]$ is detected by $\lambda^6 h_1h_4x_{109,12}$. In particular, we have 
    $$\lambda^3 \eta [h_0^2x_{124,8}] = \lambda^6 [h_1h_4x_{109,12}] \in \pi_{125,125+8} S^{0,0}$$
    for some $[h_1h_4x_{109,12}]$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:sequence
nodes.title: A spectral sequence in an abelian category
nodes.display_title: Def 1.1: A spectral sequence in an abelian category
nodes.body: Let $C$ be an abelian category and let the grading group be additive. A spectral sequence consists of nested cycle and boundary subobjects, their quotient pages, differentials of the specified degree with square zero, and compatible identifications of successor pages with homology. The same ambient data determine $E_\infty$.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:indices
nodes.title: Adams pages and extension lengths
nodes.display_title: Def 1.2: Adams pages and extension lengths
nodes.body: An Adams page carries an integer value $r\geq2$. An extension length is a nonnegative integer and may be zero. A page-level convention relates the page index, cycle level, and quotient exponent compatibly with successors. An extension length $n$ determines an Adams page when $n\geq2$.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:morphism
nodes.title: Morphisms of spectral sequences
nodes.display_title: Def 1.3: Morphisms of spectral sequences
nodes.body: A morphism preserves the ambient cycle and boundary towers and commutes with the differential. Its maps on finite pages and on $E_\infty$ are induced by this same underlying morphism.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:naturality
nodes.title: Naturality on pages and at infinity
nodes.display_title: Thm 1.4: Naturality on pages and at infinity
nodes.body: The induced page and infinity maps preserve identities and composition. On every page the induced map commutes with the actual differential.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:representatives
nodes.title: A label represented on a later page
nodes.display_title: Def 1.5: A label represented on a later page
nodes.body: For a module-valued spectral sequence, $x\in E_2^p$ represents $x_r\in E_r^p$ if one cycle representative projects to both classes. Reaching $E_r$ means such a representative exists; surviving to $E_r$ additionally requires $x_r\neq0$.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:representatives-unique
nodes.title: Uniqueness and transport of representatives
nodes.display_title: Thm 1.6: Uniqueness and transport of representatives
nodes.body: A fixed $E_2$ label has at most one represented class on a specified later page. Spectral-sequence morphisms transport representatives and differential equations through their induced page maps.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:cycles-boundaries
nodes.title: Cycles, boundaries, and incoming hits
nodes.display_title: Def 1.7: Cycles, boundaries, and incoming hits
nodes.body: A page-$r$ cycle is an element $x_r\in\ker d_r$, and a page-$r$ boundary is an element of $\operatorname{im}d_r$. A second-page label is a boundary by page $r$ if it lifts from the boundary subobject at page $r+1$; it is a final boundary if it lifts from $B_\infty$. An incoming hit on page $r$ is a differential whose represented target is nonzero.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:differential
nodes.title: Differentials between named labels
nodes.display_title: Def 1.8: Differentials between named labels
nodes.body: For $x\in E_2^p$ and $y\in E_2^q$, the relation $d_r(x)=y$ means that $q=p+\deg(d_r)$ and that there exist classes $x_r,y_r$ represented by $x,y$, respectively, satisfying $d_r(x_r)=y_r$. The differential is nonzero when $y_r\neq0$. Differential vanishing on $x$ means that every page-$r$ class represented by $x$ has zero outgoing differential; this condition also holds when $x$ has no page-$r$ representative.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:nonzero-differential
nodes.title: Consequences of a nonzero differential
nodes.display_title: Thm 1.9: Consequences of a nonzero differential
nodes.body: A nonzero differential gives nonzero representatives of both source and target on its page, hits the specified target, and implies that the actual differential morphism is nonzero.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:windows
nodes.title: Survival on a finite window
nodes.display_title: Def 1.10: Survival on a finite window
nodes.body: Let $2\leq a\leq b$. A label is a cycle on the window $[a,b]$ if, for every integer $r$ in this interval, it represents a class $x_r$ with $d_r(x_r)=0$. It survives on this window if it represents a nonzero class on every page in the interval. It is never hit on this window if no page in the interval has a nonzero incoming differential with that represented target.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:permanent
nodes.title: Permanent cycles and nonzero survival
nodes.display_title: Def 1.11: Permanent cycles and nonzero survival
nodes.body: A permanent cycle is an $E_2$ label with a common representative in $Z_\infty$. Nonzero survival requires that this representative have nonzero image in $E_\infty$. In both cases the infinite-cycle representative projects to the original $E_2$ label.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:stabilization
nodes.title: Stabilization after vanishing differentials
nodes.display_title: Thm 1.12: Stabilization after vanishing differentials
nodes.body: If all outgoing differentials at a fixed degree vanish from page $N$ onward, its cycle tower stabilizes there. If the corresponding incoming differential morphisms vanish, its boundary tower stabilizes as well. The page $N$ must be at least the initial page.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:permanence-from-finite
nodes.title: From a finite page to infinity
nodes.display_title: Thm 1.13: From a finite page to infinity
nodes.body: Let $N\geq r_0$. If a label reaches page $N$ and $d_r$ is zero on its degree for every $r\geq N$, it is a permanent cycle. If it survives nontrivially to $N$ and the incoming differential morphisms are also zero for every $r\geq N$, it has nonzero survival at infinity.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:page-three
nodes.title: The third page as a differential quotient
nodes.display_title: Thm 1.14: The third page as a differential quotient
nodes.body: Let $E$ be a module-valued spectral sequence with initial page $r_0\leq2$. A second-page class reaches $E_3$ if and only if it is a $d_2$ cycle. Two represented third-page classes agree if and only if their second-page difference lies in the image of the incoming $d_2$. A second-page label is a boundary by page two if and only if it lies in that image. Every third-page class has a second-page label.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:representative-expansion
nodes.title: Calculating from complete representatives
nodes.display_title: Thm 1.15: Calculating from complete representatives
nodes.body: Let $E$ be a spectral sequence of abelian groups, let $r\geq2$, and suppose $E_2^p\cong(\mathbb F_2)^N$ has basis $b_0,\ldots,b_{N-1}$. Suppose each $b_i$ represents $a_i\in E_r^p$. Then every page-$r$ class is a sum of a subfamily of the $a_i$. If $d_r(a_i)=0$ for every $i$, then $d_r=0$ in degree $p$. More generally, for a $\mathbb Z$-linear isomorphism $e:A\cong(\mathbb F_2)^N$, every $a\in A$ is the sum of the basis vectors whose coordinates under $e$ are nonzero.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:successor-nonzero
nodes.title: Nonzero representatives on the successor page
nodes.display_title: Thm 1.16: Nonzero representatives on the successor page
nodes.body: Suppose the same label already has represented classes on page $r$ and on page $r+1$, with $r$ at least two and at least the initial page. The successor-page representative is nonzero if the page-$r$ representative is not an incoming differential target. It is also nonzero if the page-$r$ representative is nonzero and the relevant incoming morphism vanishes.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:finite-frames
nodes.title: Small finite-page frames
nodes.display_title: Thm 1.17: Small finite-page frames
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:finite-hit
nodes.title: A differential target becomes zero later
nodes.display_title: Thm 1.18: A differential target becomes zero later
nodes.body: Suppose $r\geq r_0$ and $d_r(x)=y$ between represented second-page labels in degrees $p$ and $q=p+\deg(d_r)$. The represented page-$r$ target is a cycle. For every $t>r$, the label $y$ represents zero on page $t$.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:filtration
nodes.title: A decreasing filtration and its associated graded
nodes.display_title: Def 1.19: A decreasing filtration and its associated graded
nodes.body: A filtration consists of decreasing subobjects $F^s A^k$. Its associated graded is the cokernel of $F^{s+1}A^k\longrightarrow F^sA^k$, with its canonical quotient map. Filtration-preserving maps induce the corresponding maps on associated graded objects.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:bounded
nodes.title: Boundedness, exhaustion, and separation
nodes.display_title: Def 1.20: Boundedness, exhaustion, and separation
nodes.body: A bounded filtration has explicit lower and upper bounds in each degree. Lower boundedness implies exhaustion, and upper boundedness implies the Hausdorff property, for the same filtration.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:completion
nodes.title: The quotient tower of a filtration
nodes.display_title: Def 1.21: The quotient tower of a filtration
nodes.body: The quotients $A^k/F^sA^k$, their transition morphisms, and the canonical cone form the quotient tower. A completion witness identifies the original object with the limit of this specified tower.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:convergence
nodes.title: Convergence to a specified filtered object
nodes.display_title: Def 1.22: Convergence to a specified filtered object
nodes.body: Convergence consists of a bijective reindexing of degrees and isomorphisms $E_\infty^p\cong\operatorname{gr}^{s}A^k$ for that reindexing $p\mapsto(s,k)$. A converging spectral sequence packages the same sequence, filtered target, and comparison.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:detection
nodes.title: Detection in an associated graded quotient
nodes.display_title: Def 1.23: Detection in an associated graded quotient
nodes.body: An infinity-page class detects a filtered representative when its convergence image equals the associated graded quotient of that representative. A convergence morphism preserves the filtered target and commutes with these specified infinity-page identifications.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:detected-difference
nodes.title: Differences of detected representatives
nodes.display_title: Thm 1.24: Differences of detected representatives
nodes.body: Let $T$ be an object of the abelian category, and let $x,x' : T\to F^sA^k$ be filtered representatives. If $y:T\to E_\infty^p$ detects both, where $p$ reindexes to $(s,k)$, then $x-x'$ factors through $F^{s+1}A^k$. Conversely, if $y$ detects $x$ and this factorization exists, then $y$ detects $x'$. The zero infinity-page class detects $x$ if and only if $x$ factors through $F^{s+1}A^k$. For module-valued filtrations, a filtered element has zero associated graded image if and only if its ambient image belongs to $F^{s+1}A^k$.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:graded-vanishing
nodes.title: Vanishing associated graded pieces
nodes.display_title: Thm 1.25: Vanishing associated graded pieces
nodes.body: A zero associated graded piece makes two successive filtration subobjects equal. If all associated graded pieces in a specified interval vanish, the filtration levels at its endpoints agree.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:ambient-differential
nodes.title: Differential relations on ambient representatives
nodes.display_title: Def 1.26: Differential relations on ambient representatives
nodes.body: The ambient differential relation expresses the actual page differential through representatives in its cycle subobjects. The full set of possible targets is recorded as a boundary coset; essentiality excludes zero from that coset.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:differential-coset
nodes.title: The complete differential target coset
nodes.display_title: Thm 1.27: The complete differential target coset
nodes.body: Once a differential relation from $x$ to $y$ is known, another target $z$ satisfies the same relation exactly when it lies in the complete target coset of $y$. Essentiality is equivalently the exclusion of zero from the target coset.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:extension-equation
nodes.title: Extensions of one specified filtered map
nodes.display_title: Def 1.28: Extensions of one specified filtered map
nodes.body: Let $f:A\to B$ preserve filtrations $F,G$, and let $T$ be an object of the abelian category. A length-$n$ extension from $x:T\to\operatorname{gr}^s A$ to $y:T\to\operatorname{gr}^{s+n}B$ consists of $n\geq0$ and lifts $a:T\to F^sA$, $b:T\to G^{s+n}B$ with associated graded images $x,y$ such that $f\circ i_F\circ a=i_G\circ b$, where $i_F,i_G$ are the ambient inclusions.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:extension-ambiguity
nodes.title: Target indeterminacy and essential extensions
nodes.display_title: Def 1.29: Target indeterminacy and essential extensions
nodes.body: The target indeterminacy consists of targets of extensions from the zero source label for this same map and length. The target coset is obtained by translating that set. An extension is essential if its full target coset excludes zero.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:extension-coset
nodes.title: All targets of the same extension source
nodes.display_title: Thm 1.30: All targets of the same extension source
nodes.body: Extension relations are closed under addition and subtraction. For a known extension from $x$ to $y$, the full coset of $y$ consists exactly of all targets of $x$. Such an extension is essential exactly when $x$ has no zero target.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:higher-filtration
nodes.title: Indeterminacy from higher source filtration
nodes.display_title: Thm 1.31: Indeterminacy from higher source filtration
nodes.body: For a test object $T$, a morphism $y:T\to\operatorname{gr}^{s+n}B$ belongs to the target indeterminacy if and only if $n\geq0$ and there are lifts $a:T\to F^{s+1}A$ and $b:T\to G^{s+n}B$ such that $f\circ i_F\circ a=i_G\circ b$ and $b$ has associated graded image $y$.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:length-zero
nodes.title: Length-zero extensions
nodes.display_title: Thm 1.32: Length-zero extensions
nodes.body: At length zero, the extension relation is the equation for the induced associated graded map together with existence of a source lift. When the test object is projective, that lifting condition follows from the quotient epimorphism.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:bounded-ess
nodes.title: The bounded extension spectral sequence
nodes.display_title: Def 1.33: The bounded extension spectral sequence
nodes.body: For the same filtered map $f$, assume that both actual filtrations are bounded. Its extension spectral sequence begins on page zero and has differential degree $(n,-1)$ at page $n$ in the grading of the two-term complex. Its source and target ambient objects are the corresponding associated graded pieces of the original filtrations.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:ess-equation
nodes.title: ESS differentials are extension equations
nodes.display_title: Thm 1.34: ESS differentials are extension equations
nodes.body: For bounded source and target filtrations, a nonnegative length $n$, and a projective test object, the actual differential relation in the bounded extension spectral sequence is equivalent to the representative extension equation for the original filtered map.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:filtered-transport
nodes.title: Transport by levelwise filtered isomorphisms
nodes.display_title: Def 1.35: Transport by levelwise filtered isomorphisms
nodes.body: A filtered-piece isomorphism identifies the ambient objects and every filtration level, compatibly with inclusion. A transport of filtered maps consists of such isomorphisms on source and target making the actual ambient square commute.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:extension-transport
nodes.title: Transport preserves extensions and their full ambiguity
nodes.display_title: Thm 1.36: Transport preserves extensions and their full ambiguity
nodes.body: Levelwise filtered transport preserves representative equations, extension relations, complete target indeterminacy, target cosets, and essentiality. These representative-level statements do not require bounded filtrations.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:crossing-transport
nodes.title: Transport of crossings and ESS differentials
nodes.display_title: Thm 1.37: Transport of crossings and ESS differentials
nodes.body: A crossing is a higher-source-filtration essential extension whose target level crosses the selected bound. Such crossings are preserved by filtered transport. If all four filtrations are bounded and the test object is projective, transport also preserves the differential relation in the extension spectral sequences.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:pairing
nodes.title: Pairings of spectral sequences
nodes.display_title: Def 1.38: Pairings of spectral sequences
nodes.body: A pairing is bilinear on every page, has a specified parity and compatible differential degrees, obeys the signed Leibniz rule, and descends through the actual common-cycle successor-page relation.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:converging-pairing
nodes.title: Products from finite pages to the abutment
nodes.display_title: Def 1.39: Products from finite pages to the abutment
nodes.body: A converging pairing ties the finite-page products to one product on common infinite cycles, its induced $E_\infty$ product, the filtered abutment product, and the associated graded product. All comparisons use the same convergence isomorphisms.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:unit
nodes.title: A common-cycle unit
nodes.display_title: Def 1.40: A common-cycle unit
nodes.body: Unit data consist of an infinite cycle in degree zero and a filtration-zero abutment representative with the same associated graded image. Their projections give the specified unit classes on every finite page, on $E_\infty$, and in the abutment.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:SpectralSequence:converging-category
nodes.title: Morphisms of converging sequences
nodes.display_title: Def 1.41: Morphisms of converging sequences
nodes.body: A converging-sequence morphism includes both a full spectral-sequence morphism and a convergence morphism, with identical action on $E_\infty$. Identity and composition define a category of converging spectral sequences.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: paper:2.1
nodes.title: The extension spectral sequence
nodes.display_title: Def 1.42: The extension spectral sequence
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Definition 2.1.)


  For a map $f: X\to Y$, we define an $f$-extension spectral sequence (denoted $f$-ESS) as the spectral sequence derived from filtering the above chain complex according to the Adams filtration on $\pi_*$. The $E_0$-page of this spectral sequence is isomorphic to the direct sum of $E_\infty$-pages of the Adams spectral sequences of $X$ and $Y$: 
  $$\ESS{f}_0^{s,t} \cong E_\infty^{s,t}(X) \oplus E_\infty^{s,t}(Y) \Longrightarrow \Ker(\pi_*f)\oplus \Coker(\pi_*f)$$
  where the $d_0$-differential is induced by $f$ on the $E_\infty$-pages.
  
  Differentials in this spectral sequence has the form
  $$d_n^{f}: \ESS{f}_n^{s,t}\to \ESS{f}_n^{s+n, t+n}.$$
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: paper:2.6
nodes.title: Vanishing below the Adams filtration
nodes.display_title: Cor 1.43: Vanishing below the Adams filtration
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Corollary 2.6.)

If the Adams filtration of $f$ is $k$, then
    $d^f_i=0$ for $i<k$.
nodes.chapter: SpectralSequence --- Spectral Sequences and Extensions

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:categories
nodes.title: The fixed categories and coefficient object
nodes.display_title: Def 2.1: The fixed categories and coefficient object
nodes.body: Let $\mathrm{Sp}$ and $\mathrm{Syn}$ be the classical and synthetic stable categories, with functorial cofibers. Equip $\mathrm{Sp}$ with its closed symmetric monoidal structure, and fix the mod-two coefficient object $H\mathbb F_2$ and its unit.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
nodes.section: The fixed classical and synthetic background

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:realizations
nodes.title: Point-set realizations of the fixed categories
nodes.display_title: Def 2.2: Point-set realizations of the fixed categories
nodes.body: The classical and synthetic point-set stable categories admit localizations equivalent to $\mathrm{Sp}$ and $\mathrm{Syn}$, respectively. These equivalences identify the localization functors with the passage from point-set spectra to their homotopy classes.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
nodes.section: The fixed classical and synthetic background

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:nu
nodes.title: The synthetic analogue functor
nodes.display_title: Def 2.3: The synthetic analogue functor
nodes.body: Let $\nu\colon\mathrm{Sp}\to\mathrm{Syn}$ be the synthetic analogue functor, together with its additive structure, its sphere and zero-object identifications, and its suspension comparison maps.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
nodes.section: The fixed classical and synthetic background

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:recovery
nodes.title: Realization and recovery
nodes.display_title: Def 2.4: Realization and recovery
nodes.body: Realization $R\colon\mathrm{Syn}\to\mathrm{Sp}$ is left adjoint to the fully faithful spectral Yoneda functor. There is a natural isomorphism $R\nu\cong\operatorname{id}_{\mathrm{Sp}}$.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
nodes.section: The fixed classical and synthetic background

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:lambda-quotients
nodes.title: Finite lambda quotients
nodes.display_title: Def 2.5: Finite lambda quotients
nodes.body: For $X\in\mathrm{Syn}$ and $n\geq0$, let $X/\lambda^n$ be the cofiber of $\lambda^n$. The quotient maps and their cofiber comparisons form the finite $\lambda$-quotient system.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
nodes.section: The fixed classical and synthetic background

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:nu-exactness
nodes.title: When nu preserves a cofiber triangle
nodes.display_title: Thm 2.6: When nu preserves a cofiber triangle
nodes.body:
Let $X	o Y	o Z	o\Sigma X$ be a distinguished triangle in $\mathrm{Sp}$. If its mod-two homology forms a short exact sequence in every degree, then there exists $h\colon
u Z	o\Sigma
u X$ such that $
u X	o
u Y	o
u Z\xrightarrow{h}\Sigma
u X$ is a distinguished triangle in $\mathrm{Syn}$.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
nodes.section: The fixed classical and synthetic background

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:sphere-sign
nodes.title: The sign of the sphere twist
nodes.display_title: Thm 2.7: The sign of the sphere twist
nodes.body: For integers $r,s$, the braiding $S^r\wedge S^s\to S^s\wedge S^r$ is multiplication by $(-1)^{rs}$ under the sphere-smash identifications with $S^{r+s}$ and the identification $r+s=s+r$.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
nodes.section: The fixed classical and synthetic background

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:families
nodes.title: The classical and synthetic Adams systems
nodes.display_title: Def 2.8: The classical and synthetic Adams systems
nodes.body: The coefficient units determine functorial classical and synthetic Adams towers. Write $E_r^{s,t}(X)$ for the resulting classical bidegree spectral sequence, and use the synthetic tridegree spectral sequence for objects of $\mathrm{Syn}$.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
nodes.section: Adams towers, convergence, and finite filtration

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:synthetic-indices
nodes.title: The classical page and differential conventions
nodes.display_title: Thm 2.9: The classical page and differential conventions
nodes.body: For $X\in\mathrm{Sp}$, the Adams spectral sequence begins at $E_2$ and its page-$r$ differential has degree $(r,r-1)$. For $f\colon X\to Y$ and $g\colon Y\to Z$, one has $E(g\circ f)=E(g)\circ E(f)$.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
nodes.section: Adams towers, convergence, and finite filtration

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:selected-convergence
nodes.title: Convergence on the object families
nodes.display_title: Def 2.10: Convergence on the object families
nodes.body: For $X\in\mathcal C_0$ and $Y\in\mathcal S_0$, the coefficient-unit Adams towers converge to the Adams-filtered homotopy groups of $X$ and $Y$, respectively. Classical suspension identifies the suspended tower with the tower of the suspended object.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
nodes.section: Adams towers, convergence, and finite filtration

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:filtration-comparison
nodes.title: Two descriptions of Adams filtration
nodes.display_title: Thm 2.11: Two descriptions of Adams filtration
nodes.body: Let $f$ be a map in $\mathrm{Sp}$ and $s\in\mathbb Z$. The map $f$ has filtration at least $s$ with respect to the Adams tower of its target if and only if it has filtration at least $s$ defined by factorization into maps inducing zero in mod-two homology.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
nodes.section: Adams towers, convergence, and finite filtration

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:finite-separation
nodes.title: Separation for maps of finite spectra
nodes.display_title: Thm 2.12: Separation for maps of finite spectra
nodes.body: Let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a map between finite spectra. If $f$ lies in every integer stage of the Adams filtration, then $f$ is odd torsion. The same assertion holds for the factorization filtration. Consequently, every map between finite spectra which is not odd torsion has an exact finite integer filtration.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
nodes.section: Adams towers, convergence, and finite filtration

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:bounded-filtration
nodes.title: Bounded filtration in a fixed homotopy degree
nodes.display_title: Thm 2.13: Bounded filtration in a fixed homotopy degree
nodes.body: Let $X$ be finite, rationally acyclic, and homotopy two-local. For every $i\in\mathbb Z$, there is an integer $N$ such that $F^s\pi_i(X)=0$ for all $s\geq N$, where $F$ is the coefficient-tower Adams filtration.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
nodes.section: Adams towers, convergence, and finite filtration

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:classical-vanishing
nodes.title: Low-filtration support and sphere separation
nodes.display_title: Thm 2.14: Low-filtration support and sphere separation
nodes.body: For $X\in\mathcal C_0$, one has $E_r^{s,t}(X)=0$ whenever $s<0$. For the sphere, $E_r^{0,t}(S)=0$ for every nonzero $t\geq0$. A sphere homotopy class lying in $F^s$ for every $s\in\mathbb N$ is odd torsion.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
nodes.section: Adams towers, convergence, and finite filtration

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:homology-exact
nodes.title: Cofiber homology and a cardinality bound
nodes.display_title: Thm 2.15: Cofiber homology and a cardinality bound
nodes.body: Mod-two homology of a cofiber sequence is exact at the cofiber term, with boundary induced by the cofiber map to the suspension. Suppose that every finite subset of the two adjacent homology groups has cardinality at most $n_X$ and $n_Y$, respectively. Then every finite subset of the cofiber homology group has cardinality at most $n_Xn_Y$.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
nodes.section: Adams towers, convergence, and finite filtration

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:finite-quotient-separation
nodes.title: Separation on finite lambda quotients
nodes.display_title: Thm 2.16: Separation on finite lambda quotients
nodes.body: For $X\in\mathcal S_0$ and every finite exponent $n\geq0$, the synthetic Adams filtration on $X/\lambda^n$ is homotopy separated.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
nodes.section: Adams towers, convergence, and finite filtration

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:source-recognition
nodes.title: Recognition of the classical source
nodes.display_title: Def 2.17: Recognition of the classical source
nodes.body: The equivalence from the classical point-set homotopy category to $\mathrm{Sp}$ identifies the sphere, integer homotopy groups, the mod-two coefficient object, its coordinate, and its normalized unit. It also identifies mapping-cone inclusions and boundaries with their cofiber counterparts in $\mathrm{Sp}$.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
nodes.section: Source recognition and standard sphere classes

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:source-smash
nodes.title: Recognition of the derived smash product
nodes.display_title: Def 2.18: Recognition of the derived smash product
nodes.body: Choose a levelwise good point-set replacement naturally stably equivalent to the identity. After replacement, diagonal smash preserves stable equivalences. The generator and derived-smash comparisons identify this derived smash with the tensor product in $\mathrm{Sp}$ on the source objects for which these comparisons are defined.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
nodes.section: Source recognition and standard sphere classes

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:canonical-tower
nodes.title: The canonical coefficient-unit Adams tower
nodes.display_title: Def 2.19: The canonical coefficient-unit Adams tower
nodes.body: For $X\in\mathrm{Sp}$, define its canonical Adams tower recursively by taking fibers of the coefficient-unit maps. Its spectral sequence has the tower cycles and boundaries as cycle and boundary subgroups, with limiting cycles given by their intersection and limiting boundaries by their union.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
nodes.section: Source recognition and standard sphere classes

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:canonical-comparison
nodes.title: Comparison with the canonical tower sequence
nodes.display_title: Thm 2.20: Comparison with the canonical tower sequence
nodes.body: For every $X\in\mathrm{Sp}$, its classical Adams sequence is isomorphic to the canonical coefficient-tower sequence. This isomorphism identifies ambient groups, finite pages, differentials, infinite cycles, and infinite boundaries. For sphere classes it preserves and reflects nonzero permanent survival.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
nodes.section: Source recognition and standard sphere classes

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:hf2-localization
nodes.title: The mod-two-localized classical sequence
nodes.display_title: Def 2.21: The mod-two-localized classical sequence
nodes.body: The classical Adams functor sends mod-two homology equivalences to isomorphisms and hence factors through localization at these equivalences. The resulting localized sphere sequence is isomorphic to the ordinary classical sphere sequence; let the localized $h_6^2$ be the class corresponding to $h_6^2$ under this isomorphism.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
nodes.section: Source recognition and standard sphere classes

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:localized-survival
nodes.title: Survival across the localization comparison
nodes.display_title: Thm 2.22: Survival across the localization comparison
nodes.body: A sphere $E_2$ class survives nontrivially if and only if its image under the localized-sphere comparison survives nontrivially. The two classes correspond through a common infinite-cycle representative.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
nodes.section: Source recognition and standard sphere classes

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:milnor-coordinates
nodes.title: Milnor coordinates of the first page
nodes.display_title: Def 2.23: Milnor coordinates of the first page
nodes.body: The first differential of the canonical coefficient tower is induced by its connecting maps. Milnor coordinates identify its first-page groups with the normalized Milnor cochains. A tower cycle determines its canonical second-page class by passage to the cycle quotient.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
nodes.section: Source recognition and standard sphere classes

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:milnor-differential
nodes.title: The coordinate differential and second-page quotient
nodes.display_title: Thm 2.24: The coordinate differential and second-page quotient
nodes.body: Under Milnor coordinates, the first tower differential is the polynomial differential, so second-page tower cycles correspond exactly to cocycles. Passing to the cycle quotient and then applying the source comparison gives the sphere $E_2$ equivalence with Milnor cohomology.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
nodes.section: Source recognition and standard sphere classes

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:milnor-products
nodes.title: The sphere product in Milnor cohomology
nodes.display_title: Thm 2.25: The sphere product in Milnor cohomology
nodes.body: The Milnor equivalence identifies the sphere $E_2$ product with the normalized cobar cup product and sends the sphere unit to the cohomology unit. The sphere product satisfies the corresponding commutativity law.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
nodes.section: Source recognition and standard sphere classes

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:standard-classes
nodes.title: The standard sphere classes
nodes.display_title: Def 2.26: The standard sphere classes
nodes.body: Let $h_i\in E_2^{1,2^i}(S)$ be the classes of the standard Milnor cocycles. Define $h_6^2\in E_2^{2,128}(S)$ as the product of $h_6$ with itself. Under the Milnor equivalence, $h_6^2$ is the cup square of the cocycle class defining $h_6$.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework
nodes.section: Source recognition and standard sphere classes

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:mapping-spectra
nodes.title: Adams sequences of finite mapping spectra
nodes.display_title: Def 2.27: Adams sequences of finite mapping spectra
nodes.body: For finite spectra $X,Y$, let $F(X,Y)$ be the internal hom in $\mathrm{Sp}$. Its coefficient-unit tower and convergence to its homotopy filtration define the mapping-spectrum Adams sequence.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:mapping-detection
nodes.title: Detection of maps in the mapping spectral sequence
nodes.display_title: Thm 2.28: Detection of maps in the mapping spectral sequence
nodes.body: For finite spectra $X,Y$, the Adams filtration of $f\colon X\to Y$ equals that of its class in $\pi_0F(X,Y)$. Exact filtration is detected by the convergence quotient comparison. If $f$ is not odd torsion, it has a nonzero $E_\infty$ detector represented by a common infinite cycle.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:mapping-pairing
nodes.title: Composition pairings of mapping sequences
nodes.display_title: Def 2.29: Composition pairings of mapping sequences
nodes.body: For finite spectra $X,Y,Z$, composition induces a converging pairing from the Adams sequences of $F(X,Y)$ and $F(Y,Z)$ to that of $F(X,Z)$. Its parity is the Adams stem parity, and its abutment pairing is shifted composition in $\mathrm{Sp}$.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:mapping-laws
nodes.title: Associativity and units for mapping composition
nodes.display_title: Thm 2.30: Associativity and units for mapping composition
nodes.body: The finite-page mapping pairings are associative under the degree identifications and have compatible left and right units. Each unit is represented by a common infinite cycle whose abutment is the identity map.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:mapping-sphere
nodes.title: The sphere specialization of mapping composition
nodes.display_title: Thm 2.31: The sphere specialization of mapping composition
nodes.body: Under the closed-unit identification of the sphere mapping sequence with the sphere Adams sequence, composition and identity correspond to the sphere $E_2$ product and unit.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:mapping-enrichment
nodes.title: Enrichment by converging spectral sequences
nodes.display_title: Def 2.32: Enrichment by converging spectral sequences
nodes.body: The finite spectra form a category enriched in the monoidal category of converging spectral sequences. Its hom objects are the mapping-spectrum Adams sequences, with the composition pairings and identity units above.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:enriched-composition
nodes.title: Enriched composition agrees on all three layers
nodes.display_title: Thm 2.33: Enriched composition agrees on all three layers
nodes.body: On elementary products, enriched composition agrees with the mapping composition pairing on every finite page, on $E_\infty$, and on the abutment. The enriched identities agree with the mapping units on each of these three levels.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:graded-hom
nodes.title: Weight-graded synthetic hom groups
nodes.display_title: Def 2.34: Weight-graded synthetic hom groups
nodes.body: For synthetic spectra $X,Y$, put $\operatorname{Hom}_w(X,Y)=\operatorname{Hom}(\Sigma^{0,w}X,Y)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_*(X,Y)=\bigoplus_w\operatorname{Hom}_w(X,Y)$. The total hom group is a $\mathbb Z[\lambda]$-module; multiplication by $\lambda$ lowers weight by one through the shift comparison.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:graded-composition
nodes.title: Composition in the weight-graded enrichment
nodes.display_title: Thm 2.35: Composition in the weight-graded enrichment
nodes.body: Composition on the weight-graded hom groups is $\mathbb Z[\lambda]$-bilinear. On homogeneous summands it is shifted composition. Under the coherent shift identifications, it is associative and the identity maps are left and right units.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:e2-comparison
nodes.title: The classical-to-synthetic second-page comparison
nodes.display_title: Def 2.36: The classical-to-synthetic second-page comparison
nodes.body: The classical-to-synthetic comparison identifies classical $E_2$ classes with synthetic $E_2$ classes at the corresponding weights. The image of the corresponding synthetic $E_2$ label under the quotient page map detects the first $\lambda$-quotient homotopy class. For the sphere, this identification is compatible with the quotient map and powers of $\lambda$ through their detection identities.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:first-quotient-shifts
nodes.title: First-quotient labels and suspension
nodes.display_title: Thm 2.37: First-quotient labels and suspension
nodes.body: The first-quotient identification commutes with positive weight shift and classical suspension under the classical and synthetic suspension comparisons.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:normalized-map
nodes.title: Normalized synthetic maps
nodes.display_title: Def 2.38: Normalized synthetic maps
nodes.body: For a map $f$ between objects of $\mathcal C_0$, its normalized synthetic lift is obtained from $\nu(f)$ with exponent determined by whether $f$ factors through the first stage of the target Adams tower. Composing this lift with the corresponding power of $\lambda$ gives $\nu(f)$. Every map between objects of $\mathcal S_0$ induces a morphism of converging Adams sequences.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:shift-coherence
nodes.title: Coherence of synthetic shifts and lambda
nodes.display_title: Thm 2.39: Coherence of synthetic shifts and lambda
nodes.body: The bidegree-shift comparison satisfies associativity and both unit laws. It commutes with $\lambda$ under the sum-degree identifications, and the bidegree-shift functors are additive.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:weight-maps
nodes.title: Maps which lower synthetic weight
nodes.display_title: Def 2.40: Maps which lower synthetic weight
nodes.body: Let $X\in\mathcal C_0$ and $w_1\leq w_2\leq t$. The weight-lowering map on $E_\infty$ sends weight $w_2$ to weight $w_1$. It carries representatives of a classical class at weight $w_2$ to representatives of the same class at weight $w_1$.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:weight-functoriality
nodes.title: Functoriality and naturality of weight maps
nodes.display_title: Thm 2.41: Functoriality and naturality of weight maps
nodes.body: Weight-lowering maps are identities at equal weights and compose along ordered weights. For $w_1\leq w_2\leq t$, they commute with the $E_\infty$ maps induced by $\nu(f)$.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:ess-shifts
nodes.title: Shift comparisons for synthetic extensions
nodes.display_title: Def 2.42: Shift comparisons for synthetic extensions
nodes.body: For objects of $\mathcal S_0$, bidegree shifts induce compatible filtered-homotopy and finite-page identifications. In particular, the shifts $\Sigma^{1,-n}$ give shift comparisons for the extension spectral sequences, including those of finite $\lambda$ quotients.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: sem:AdamsSynthetic:shift-representatives
nodes.title: Shift transport of common representatives
nodes.display_title: Thm 2.43: Shift transport of common representatives
nodes.body: Let $r\geq2$ be a finite page. Under the synthetic shift comparison, two shifted classes have a common representative if and only if the corresponding unshifted classes do, using the induced filtered map on homotopy groups.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: paper:3.3
nodes.title: The class $\lambda$ and its cofibers
nodes.display_title: Def 2.44: The class $\lambda$ and its cofibers
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Definition 3.3.)

[{\cite{Pst} ([Definition 4.27])}]
    The natural comparison map
    $$S^{0,-1}=\Sus \nu (S^{-1})\to \nu(\Sus S^{-1})=S^{0,0}$$
    in the category of $\HF$-synthetic spectra is denoted by $\lambda\in \pi_{0,-1}S^{0,0}$. We denote by $S^{0,0}/\lambda$ the cofiber of $\lambda$. In general for synthetic $X$ the following
    $$\lambda\wedge id_X: \Sus^{0,-1}X\to X.$$
    is a natural transformation and by abuse of notation this map is also denoted by $\lambda$.
    We denote by $X/\lambda$ the cofiber of $\lambda$
    which is equivalent to $(S^{0,0}/\lambda) \wedge X$.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: paper:2.3
nodes.title: Extensions and essential extensions
nodes.display_title: Def 2.45: Extensions and essential extensions
nodes.body:
(From \cite{LWX126}, Definition 2.3.)


    We say there is an $f$-extension from $x\in E_\infty^{s,t}(X)$ to $y\in E_\infty^{s+n,t+n}(Y)$ if $d_n^{f}(x)=y$ in the $f$-ESS. We say this $f$-extension is $\textbf{essential}$ if $y$ is nontrivial in the $E_n$-page of the $f$-ESS, or equivalently $$y\notin \BESS{f}^{s+n,t+n}_{n-1}(Y).$$
    Otherwise we refer to it as inessential.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: paper:2.5
nodes.title: Representatives and indeterminacy of extensions
nodes.display_title: Prop 2.46: Representatives and indeterminacy of extensions
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:0895d4999173
nodes.title: Auxiliary maps and a detecting spectrum
nodes.display_title: Def 2.47: Auxiliary maps and a detecting spectrum
nodes.body: Fix maps $\eta\colon S^1\to S$ and $\nu_3\colon S^3\to S$, a spectrum $D$, and a map $S\to D$. These determine the classical object family $\mathcal C_0$ and the synthetic object family $\mathcal S_0$ defined above.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:a5b004b4748d
nodes.title: Classical and synthetic second-page comparisons
nodes.display_title: Def 2.48: Classical and synthetic second-page comparisons
nodes.body:
For $X\in\mathcal C_0$, $a,s,t\in\mathbb Z$, and $k\in\mathbb N$, there are linear isomorphisms
\[
K_{X,a,k}\colon E_2^{s,t}(X)\cong E_2^{s,t,t+a-k}(\Sigma^{0,a}\nu X),\qquad
K_{S,k}\colon E_2^{s,t}(S)\cong E_2^{s,t,t-k}(S^{0,0}).
\]
They commute with maps between objects of $\mathcal C_0$. The sphere comparison agrees with the $X=S$, $a=0$ comparison under $\nu S\cong S^{0,0}$, and the map induced by $\lambda$ sends $K_{X,-1,k}(x)$ to $K_{X,0,k+1}(x)$.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:14d5e6606bc5
nodes.title: Classical coefficient-unit towers
nodes.display_title: Def 2.49: Classical coefficient-unit towers
nodes.body: For every $X\in\mathrm{Sp}$, let $T(X)$ be its Adams tower for the unit $S\to H\mathbb F_2$. The towers are functorial in $X$. Their cycle and boundary quotients identify with the classical Adams pages, including their differentials and infinite cycles and boundaries. Under the ambient-group comparisons, induced maps agree with the maps on tower layers.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:9a4b26f47efd
nodes.title: Classical convergence and suspension
nodes.display_title: Def 2.50: Classical convergence and suspension
nodes.body:
For $X\in\mathcal C_0$, the classical Adams sequence has canonical isomorphisms
\[
E_\infty^{s,t}(X)\cong\operatorname{gr}_F^s\pi_{t-s}X.
\]
The isomorphisms identify the class of an infinite cycle represented by a tower lift with the associated graded class of the projection of that same lift. The tower of $\Sigma X$ is isomorphic stagewise and layerwise to the suspension of the tower of $X$. These isomorphisms commute with tower maps, the stage-zero comparison, and layer inclusions; the layer connecting maps commute with a minus sign under the suspension-interchange comparison.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:23334467e67d
nodes.title: Classical functorial cofibers
nodes.display_title: Def 2.51: Classical functorial cofibers
nodes.body: For $f\colon X\to Y$ in $\mathrm{Sp}$, choose a cofiber $C(f)$ with a distinguished triangle $X\xrightarrow f Y\to C(f)\to\Sigma X$. Every commutative square between such maps induces a map of cofibers commuting with the inclusions and boundaries.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:dfe52f1f4fa8
nodes.title: Comparison with the canonical Adams sequence
nodes.display_title: Def 2.52: Comparison with the canonical Adams sequence
nodes.body: For every $X\in\mathrm{Sp}$, there is an isomorphism between its classical Adams sequence and the sequence of its canonical coefficient-unit tower. The isomorphism includes the ambient groups, cycles, boundaries, finite pages, differentials, and infinite cycles and boundaries.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:96311a094390
nodes.title: Convergence for finite mapping spectra
nodes.display_title: Def 2.53: Convergence for finite mapping spectra
nodes.body:
Let $X,Y\in\mathrm{Sp}$ be finite. The Adams tower of $F(X,Y)$ has canonical isomorphisms
\[
E_\infty^{s,t}F(X,Y)\cong\operatorname{gr}_F^s\pi_{t-s}F(X,Y),
\]
identifying an infinite-cycle tower representative with the associated graded class of its projected homotopy lift.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:2fc8b595d232
nodes.title: Converging mapping pairings
nodes.display_title: Def 2.54: Converging mapping pairings
nodes.body:
For finite spectra $X,Y,Z$, let $M(X,Y)$ be the converging Adams sequence of $F(X,Y)$. There is a converging pairing
\[
P_{X,Y,Z}\colon M(X,Y)\times M(Y,Z)\longrightarrow M(X,Z).
\]
It consists of compatible pairings of pages, infinite cycles, $E_\infty$, filtered abutments, and associated graded groups; the convergence isomorphisms identify the $E_\infty$ pairing with the associated graded pairing.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:3b6637d8abc6
nodes.title: Elementary tensor pairings
nodes.display_title: Def 2.55: Elementary tensor pairings
nodes.body:
For finite spectra $X,Y,Z$, there is a converging pairing
\[
T_{X,Y,Z}\colon M(X,Y)\times M(Y,Z)\longrightarrow M(X,Y)\otimes M(Y,Z).
\]
Its finite-page, infinite-cycle, $E_\infty$, filtered-abutment, and associated-graded pairings commute with the quotient, inclusion, and convergence maps.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:84529392feed
nodes.title: Enrichment of finite spectra
nodes.display_title: Def 2.56: Enrichment of finite spectra
nodes.body: The finite spectra admit an enrichment in the monoidal category of converging spectral sequences, with enriched composition and identity morphisms satisfying the enriched associativity and unit laws.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:d505f4e20090
nodes.title: Exact shifts and realization
nodes.display_title: Def 2.57: Exact shifts and realization
nodes.body: The categories $\mathrm{Sp}$ and $\mathrm{Syn}$ are triangulated. Each bidegree shift on $\mathrm{Syn}$ is additive, commutes with integer suspension, and is exact for those suspension comparisons. Realization $R\colon\mathrm{Syn}\to\mathrm{Sp}$ commutes with suspension and is exact for its suspension comparison.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:63b3daf63e20
nodes.title: Filtered synthetic shift comparisons
nodes.display_title: Def 2.58: Filtered synthetic shift comparisons
nodes.body: For $X\in\mathcal S_0$ and $p,\delta\in\mathbb Z^2$, there is an isomorphism between the filtered homotopy group in degree $p$ of $X$ and that in degree $p+\delta$ of $\Sigma^\delta X$. It identifies the ambient groups and every filtration stage.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:f3257e955b3d
nodes.title: Finite-page synthetic shift comparisons
nodes.display_title: Def 2.59: Finite-page synthetic shift comparisons
nodes.body:
For $X\in\mathcal S_0$, $p,\delta\in\mathbb Z^2$, $s\in\mathbb Z$, and $r\geq2$, there is an isomorphism
\[
E_r^{s,p_1+s,p_2}(X)\cong E_r^{s,(p+\delta)_1+s,(p+\delta)_2}(\Sigma^\delta X).
\]
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:7bd1ea96b79a
nodes.title: First-page Milnor coordinates
nodes.display_title: Def 2.60: First-page Milnor coordinates
nodes.body:
For $s,t\in\mathbb N$, there is a $\mathbb Z$-linear isomorphism
\[
\phi_{s,t}\colon E_1^{s,t}(T(S))\cong C^{s,t}_{\mathrm{Milnor}},
\]
where the left side is the first layer group of the canonical coefficient-unit tower and the right side is the normalized Milnor cochain group.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:4d1e8d566e6a
nodes.title: Good replacement of prespectra
nodes.display_title: Def 2.61: Good replacement of prespectra
nodes.body: There is a functor $R$ on classical prespectra and a natural transformation $R\to\operatorname{id}$ such that $RX$ is levelwise good for every $X$, and every comparison $RX\to X$ is a stable equivalence.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:740de17a7d73
nodes.title: Homotopy of the first lambda quotient
nodes.display_title: Def 2.62: Homotopy of the first lambda quotient
nodes.body:
For $X\in\mathcal C_0$ and $a,s,t\in\mathbb Z$, there is a $\mathbb Z$-linear isomorphism
\[
\pi_{t-s,t+a}\bigl((\Sigma^{0,a}\nu X)/\lambda\bigr)\cong E_2^{s,t}(X).
\]
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:8e642612876d
nodes.title: Normalized synthetic lifts
nodes.display_title: Def 2.63: Normalized synthetic lifts
nodes.body:
Let $X,Y\in\mathcal C_0$ and $f\colon X\to Y$. Put $\epsilon(f)=1$ if $f$ factors through the first stage of the target Adams tower, and put $\epsilon(f)=0$ otherwise. A normalized lift is a map
\[
\widehat f\colon\Sigma^{0,\epsilon(f)}\nu X\longrightarrow\nu Y
\]
such that $\widehat f\circ\lambda^{\epsilon(f)}=\nu(f)$, using the positive-target form of the power of $\lambda$.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:5934d2f3caff
nodes.title: Point-set realizations, cofibers, and smash products
nodes.display_title: Def 2.64: Point-set realizations, cofibers, and smash products
nodes.body:
The classical and synthetic categories have stable point-set model realizations whose homotopy categories are equivalent to $\mathrm{Sp}$ and $\mathrm{Syn}$, respectively. The classical model is closed symmetric monoidal, complete, cocomplete, and cofibrantly generated; its model tensor is compatible with the model structure. On cofibrant inputs, localization identifies its tensor with the tensor in $\mathrm{Sp}$, naturally in both inputs, and sends a cofibrant replacement of its unit to $S$.

Write $Q$ for passage from classical prespectra to $\mathrm{Sp}$ under the source equivalence. For well-based prespectra $X,Y$ and $f\colon X\to Y$, there is an isomorphism $Q\operatorname{Cone}(f)\cong C(Qf)$ commuting with the cone inclusion and boundary. For good based spaces $A,B$, there is a natural isomorphism $Q\Sigma^\infty A\otimes Q\Sigma^\infty B\cong Q\Sigma^\infty(A\wedge B)$ compatible with the left unit. For all prespectra $X,Y$, the tensor $QX\otimes QY$ is naturally isomorphic to $Q(RX\wedge_{\mathrm{diag}}RY)$, where $R$ is the good replacement functor.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:e1d0c165854d
nodes.title: Recognition of classical stable homotopy
nodes.display_title: Def 2.65: Recognition of classical stable homotopy
nodes.body: The ordinary stable localization of sequential prespectra is equivalent to $\mathrm{Sp}$. Under this equivalence, the source sphere corresponds to $S$, its identity to the positive sphere generator, and integer stable homotopy groups correspond naturally to the homotopy groups in $\mathrm{Sp}$, preserving zero and stable addition. The equivalence commutes naturally with desuspension and with suspension of well-based prespectra. A source mod-two coefficient prespectrum corresponds to $H\mathbb F_2$, with the same zeroth-homotopy coordinate, vanishing in nonzero degrees, and normalized coefficient unit.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:68731f808d69
nodes.title: Recovery by lambda localization
nodes.display_title: Def 2.66: Recovery by lambda localization
nodes.body: The full subcategory of $\mathrm{Syn}$ on objects for which $\lambda$ is invertible is reflective. Let $L$ be its reflector. There is an equivalence $\mathrm{Syn}[\lambda^{-1}]\simeq\mathrm{Sp}$ under which $L\nu$ is naturally isomorphic to the inverse equivalence.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:1b85f123880c
nodes.title: Synthetic coefficient-unit towers
nodes.display_title: Def 2.67: Synthetic coefficient-unit towers
nodes.body: For every $Y\in\mathrm{Syn}$, let $T_{\mathrm{syn}}(Y)$ be its Adams tower for the image under $\nu$ of the mod-two coefficient unit. At weight $w$, the synthetic Adams sequence identifies with the tower sequence of $\Sigma^{0,-w}Y$, including its differentials, cycles, and boundaries. These identifications are functorial on $E_2$: the two ambient representatives associated to a map differ by an initial tower boundary.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:f083536a377e
nodes.title: Synthetic convergence
nodes.display_title: Def 2.68: Synthetic convergence
nodes.body:
For $Y\in\mathcal S_0$, there are canonical isomorphisms
\[
E_\infty^{s,t,w}(Y)\cong\operatorname{gr}_F^s\pi_{t-s,w}Y.
\]
The filtration agrees with the tower filtration after weight desuspension. If an infinite cycle is represented by a tower lift, its image under this isomorphism is the associated graded class of the projection of that same lift.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:c264cb4f3291
nodes.title: Synthetic functorial cofibers
nodes.display_title: Def 2.69: Synthetic functorial cofibers
nodes.body: For $f\colon X\to Y$ in $\mathrm{Syn}$, choose a cofiber $C(f)$ and a distinguished triangle $X\xrightarrow f Y\to C(f)\to\Sigma X$. A commutative square induces a map of these cofibers commuting with inclusion and boundary.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:17c9809bc74d
nodes.title: Tensor products of converging sequences
nodes.display_title: Def 2.70: Tensor products of converging sequences
nodes.body: Equip the category of converging, bigraded spectral sequences of abelian groups with a monoidal structure, with tensor product denoted by $\otimes$ and tensor unit denoted by $\mathbf 1$.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:48bf5d838430
nodes.title: The classical Adams functor
nodes.display_title: Def 2.71: The classical Adams functor
nodes.body: Let $E$ be the functor from $\mathrm{Sp}$ to bigraded spectral sequences of abelian groups. Its first page is $E_2$, and its page-$r$ differential has degree $(r,r-1)$.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:6793885d9e9c
nodes.title: The classical stable category
nodes.display_title: Def 2.72: The classical stable category
nodes.body: Equip $\mathrm{Sp}$ with a category structure with small hom sets, a preadditive structure, integer suspension functors, a monoidal structure, a zero object, and a pretriangulated structure. Each integer suspension functor is additive.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:6a2402d27721
nodes.title: The closed symmetric tensor structure
nodes.display_title: Def 2.73: The closed symmetric tensor structure
nodes.body: The monoidal category $\mathrm{Sp}$ is symmetric and closed. For each $W$, tensoring on the right with $W$ and taking the internal hom $F(W,-)$ commute with integer suspension and preserve distinguished triangles for these suspension comparisons.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:bceac53496b8
nodes.title: The converging tensor-unit class
nodes.display_title: Def 2.74: The converging tensor-unit class
nodes.body: The tensor unit $\mathbf 1$ carries an infinite cycle of degree $(0,0)$ and a filtration-zero element of its degree-zero abutment. Their associated graded classes agree under convergence, giving compatible unit classes on finite pages and on $E_\infty$.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:afb5017e1acf
nodes.title: The designated Hopf classes
nodes.display_title: Def 2.75: The designated Hopf classes
nodes.body: For every $i\in\mathbb N$, choose a class $h_i\in E_2^{1,2^i}(S)$.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:e9439d4312f5
nodes.title: The mod-two coefficient object
nodes.display_title: Def 2.76: The mod-two coefficient object
nodes.body: Choose $H\mathbb F_2\in\mathrm{Sp}$ together with an additive isomorphism $\pi_0H\mathbb F_2\cong\mathbb Z/2$ and $\pi_nH\mathbb F_2=0$ for every nonzero integer $n$. Its coefficient unit $S\to H\mathbb F_2$ is the class corresponding to $1\in\mathbb Z/2$.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:5833df0c640f
nodes.title: The objects of the classical category
nodes.display_title: Def 2.77: The objects of the classical category
nodes.body: Let $\mathrm{Sp}$ denote the type of classical spectra, in universe $\mathrm{Type}_1$.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:eaf500baffc5
nodes.title: The objects of the synthetic category
nodes.display_title: Def 2.78: The objects of the synthetic category
nodes.body: Let $\mathrm{Syn}$ denote the type of synthetic spectra, in universe $\mathrm{Type}_1$.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:8b66ee46e41e
nodes.title: The second page in Milnor coordinates
nodes.display_title: Def 2.79: The second page in Milnor coordinates
nodes.body: For $s,t\in\mathbb N$, there is a $\mathbb Z$-linear isomorphism $\Phi_{s,t}\colon E_2^{s,t}(S)\cong H^{s,t}_{\mathrm{Milnor}}$, where the group on the right is the cohomology of the normalized Milnor cobar complex.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:f05463b82afe
nodes.title: The sphere second-page algebra
nodes.display_title: Def 2.80: The sphere second-page algebra
nodes.body:
Each group $E_2^{s,t}(S)$ is an $\mathbb F_2$-module. The sphere second page has a $\mathbb Z$-bilinear product
\[
E_2^p(S)\times E_2^q(S)\longrightarrow E_2^{p+q}(S)
\]
and a unit in degree $(0,0)$. Under the identifications of equal degree sums, the product is associative and the unit is both a left and a right identity.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:46d2c66c5a63
nodes.title: The synthetic Adams functor
nodes.display_title: Def 2.81: The synthetic Adams functor
nodes.body: Let $E^{\mathrm{syn}}$ be the functor from $\mathrm{Syn}$ to trigraded spectral sequences of abelian groups. Its first page is $E_2$, and its page-$r$ differential has degree $(r,r-1,0)$.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:a9091f3f5cf2
nodes.title: The synthetic stable category
nodes.display_title: Def 2.82: The synthetic stable category
nodes.body: Equip $\mathrm{Syn}$ with a preadditive, monoidal, pretriangulated category structure, a zero object, and additive integer suspension. For $p\in\mathbb Z^2$, the fully faithful functor $\Sigma^p$ has comparisons $\Sigma^q\Sigma^p\cong\Sigma^{p+q}$, $\Sigma^{0,0}\cong\operatorname{id}$, and $\Sigma^{n,0}\cong\Sigma^n$. There is a natural transformation $\lambda\colon\Sigma^{0,-1}\to\operatorname{id}$, and natural comparisons $\Sigma^p(X\otimes Y)\cong(\Sigma^pX)\otimes Y$.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:798ab66d363c
nodes.title: Units of mapping sequences
nodes.display_title: Def 2.83: Units of mapping sequences
nodes.body: For every finite spectrum $X$, choose an infinite cycle $u_X$ of degree $(0,0)$ in $M(X,X)$ and an element of filtration zero in its degree-zero abutment. Their images agree in the associated graded group under convergence. They determine compatible classes on every finite page and on $E_\infty$.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:110602630fd8
nodes.title: Weight-lowering maps
nodes.display_title: Def 2.84: Weight-lowering maps
nodes.body:
For $X\in\mathcal C_0$ and $s,t,w_1,w_2\in\mathbb Z$ with $w_1\leq w_2\leq t$, let
\[
W_{w_2,w_1}\colon E_\infty^{s,t,w_2}(\nu X)\longrightarrow E_\infty^{s,t,w_1}(\nu X)
\]
be the weight-lowering homomorphism.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:b1eb322c2456
nodes.title: Associativity and units of mapping pairings
nodes.display_title: Thm 2.85: Associativity and units of mapping pairings
nodes.body:
For finite spectra $W,X,Y,Z$, page $r\in\mathbb Z$, and page classes $x\in M_r^i(W,X)$, $y\in M_r^j(X,Y)$, and $z\in M_r^k(Y,Z)$, one has
\[
P_r(P_r(x,y),z)=P_r(x,P_r(y,z))
\]
under the identifications of the two degree sums. For finite $X,Y$ and $x\in M_r^k(X,Y)$, the mapping-unit classes satisfy $P_r(u_X,x)=x=P_r(x,u_Y)$ under the zero-degree identifications. The abutment of $u_X$ corresponds to $\operatorname{id}_X\in\pi_0F(X,X)$.
nodes.chapter: AdamsSynthetic --- The Adams and Synthetic Framework

nodes.label: frontier:AdamsSynthetic:791f3c0e6a4a
nodes.title: Detection, products, and exactness of the synthetic analogue
nodes.display_title: Thm 2.86: Detection, products, and exactness of the synthetic analogue
nodes.body:
For $X\in\mathcal C_0$, $a,s,t\in\mathbb Z$, and $x\in E_2^{s,t}(X)$, the image of $K_{X,a,0}(x)$ under the first-quotient inclusion detects the inverse image of $x$ in $\pi_{t-s,t+a}((\Sigma^{0,a}\nu X)/\lambda)$.

For a distinguished triangle $X\to Y\to Z\to\Sigma X$ whose mod-two homology is short exact in every degree, there is a boundary $\nu Z\to\Sigma\nu X$ making the images of its first two maps a distinguished synthetic triangle.

For $s,t\in\mathbb Z$, $k\in\mathbb N$, and $\alpha\in\pi_{t-s,t}S^{0,0}$, the class $K_{S,k}(q\alpha)$ detects $\lambda^k\alpha$, where $q\alpha$ denotes the classical $E_2$ class obtained from $\alpha$ by the first-quotient comparison.

For $s,t,s',t',k,l\in\mathbb N$, $x\in E_2^{s,t}(S)$, and $y\in E_2^{s',t'}(S)$, if $K_{S,k}(x)$ detects $\alpha\in\pi_{t-s,t-k}S^{0,0}$ and $K_{S,l}(y)$ detects $\beta\in\pi_{t'-s',t'-l}S^{0,0}$, then $K_{S,k+l}(xy)$ detects $\alpha\beta$ after regrading the degree sums. For $\alpha\in\pi_{m,n}S^{0,0}$ and $\beta\in\pi_{k,l}S^{0,0}$, where $m,n,k,l\in\mathbb Z$, one has $\alpha\beta=(-1)^{mk}\beta\alpha$ after the sum-degree identifications.
